items.title: 代码如何抵达我们的服务器
items.text:
用户的浏览器首先与亚马逊 CDN 服务 CloudFront 通信，CloudFront 托管着两个独立的分发网络： * godbolt.org：将请求传递给我们的负载均衡器，同时处理压缩和缓存。 * static.ce-cdn.net：分发较重的静态资源，例如编译好的 JavaScript、图像以及 Monaco（负责语法高亮的 VS Code 编辑器组件）。

Your browser first talks to CloudFront, Amazon's CDN, which manages two separate distributions: * godbolt.org: Passes requests to our load balancer while handling compression and caching. * static.ce-cdn.net: Delivers bulky static assets like compiled JavaScript, images, and Monaco (the VS Code editor component responsible for syntax highlighting).

位于 CloudFront 前端的是 WAF（Web 应用防火墙），它设置了较高的速率限制门槛，以防止误封共用单一 NAT 地址的 C++ 培训班或课堂。

Sitting in front of CloudFront is WAF (Web Application Firewall), handling rate limiting with high thresholds to prevent blocking C++ trainers and classrooms sharing a single NAT.

items.title: 单个负载均衡器背后的众多集群
items.text:
CloudFront 后方挂载着单个 应用负载均衡器 (ALB)，根据 URL 路径将流量路由到特定集群： * 生产集群： 处理绝大部分的核心流量。 * /beta* 与 /staging*： 用于预部署检查和实验性测试。 * /winprod*： 运行 MSVC 的 Windows 实例。 * /aarch64prod*： ARM64 Graviton 架构机器。 * /gpu*： 配备真实 NVIDIA 显卡的高端机器。

Behind CloudFront sits a single Application Load Balancer (ALB), which routes traffic to specific clusters based on URL paths: * Production fleet: Handles the overwhelming bulk of traffic. * /beta* & /staging*: Used for pre-deploy checks and experiments. * /winprod*: Windows instances running MSVC. * /aarch64prod*: ARM64 Graviton machines. * /gpu*: High-end machines equipped with real NVIDIA cards.

每个集群由采用蓝/绿部署模式的 Auto Scaling Group（自动扩缩容组） 支持。扩缩容根据平均 CPU 负载动态进行。

Each fleet is backed by an Auto Scaling Group arranged in a blue/green deployment model. Scaling is handled dynamically based on average CPU loads.

items.title: 为什么编译器才是最难的部分
items.text:
Compiler Explorer 大量囤积二进制文件以防止链接失效，目前管理着跨 93 种语言的约 6,000 个编译器。

Compiler Explorer hoards binaries to prevent link rot, currently managing around 6,000 compilers across 93 languages.

为了规避 Amazon 弹性文件系统（EFS）的延迟问题，编译器被存储为压缩的只读 SquashFS 镜像，并通过 loopback 设备挂载。此外，引入 CEFS（打成约 20GB 的内容寻址镜像包，通过 autofs 按需挂载）后，操作系统启动时间从 50 秒缩短到了 20 秒。

To bypass the latency of Amazon's elastic NFS (EFS), compilers are stored as compressed, read-only SquashFS images mounted via loopback devices. Furthermore, the introduction of CEFS—content-addressed images packed into ~20GB bundles mounted on-demand via autofs—reduced OS startup times from 50 seconds to 20 seconds.

items.title: 文章背景与核心概要
items.text: 在软件工程领域，Python Wheels、Homebrew Bottles 和 OCI 容器镜像（Container Images）是三大主流的自助式二进制包分发系统。尽管它们各自在不同的技术生态中独立演进，但底层均采用了不可变、带校验和的文件制品，并通过客户端平台标签进行匹配选择。本文深度比较了这三种分发系统在元数据管理、依赖解析、回退机制上的异同，并剖析了将 OCI 注册表作为通用存储后端以及引入统一签名（Sigstore）与 GPU 硬件标签的最新技术趋势。
path: Wheels、Bottles 与容器镜像：二进制分发技术的演进与现状

items.title: 概要
items.text:
本文探讨了三大主流自助式二进制分发系统的融合趋势：Python Wheels、Homebrew Bottles 和 OCI 容器镜像。虽然这些系统是独立演进以服务于不同的技术生态系统，但它们共享一个基本架构：由客户端平台标签选择的不可变、带校验和的构建制品。文章审视了这些系统如何处理元数据、依赖解析，以及利用 OCI 注册表作为各种二进制格式通用存储后端的日益增长的趋势。

This article explores the convergence of three major self-service binary distribution systems: Python Wheels, Homebrew Bottles, and OCI Container Images. While these systems evolved independently to serve different ecosystems, they share a fundamental architecture: immutable, checksummed artifacts selected by client-side platform tags. The piece examines how these systems handle metadata, dependency resolution, and the growing trend of using OCI registries as a universal storage backend for diverse binary formats.
path: Wheels、Bottles 与容器镜像：二进制分发技术的演进与现状

items.title: 共同点与技术交集
items.text:
尽管来源各异，但这三种系统共享着相同的技术基石：

Despite their different origins, these three systems share a common technical foundation:

  • 内容寻址存储： 三者均通过 HTTP 分发不可变、带校验和的文件（zip/tar.gz）。制品一旦发布便绝不修改，更新通过发布新版本来处理。
  • 客户端匹配选择： 客户端（pip、brew 或容器运行时）负责检查宿主环境，并根据平台标签（CPU、操作系统、ABI）选择合适的制品。
  • 索引与存储解耦： 索引（列出可用文件）与存储（托管文件）互相分离。这带来了极高的架构灵活性，例如从 Bintray 迁移到 GitHub Packages，或者通过简单的 HTTP 缓存进行镜像分发。
  • 元数据打包： 每种格式都捆绑了一个元数据文档（如 .dist-info、INSTALL_RECEIPT.json 或 OCI 配置对象），用于记录构建细节和来源出处。
  • Content-Addressed Storage: All three distribute immutable, checksummed files (zip/tar.gz) via HTTP. Once published, artifacts are never modified; updates are handled by shipping new versions.
  • Client-Side Selection: The client (pip, brew, or a container runtime) is responsible for inspecting the host environment and selecting the appropriate artifact based on platform tags (CPU, OS, ABI).
  • Decoupled Indexing: The index (which lists available files) is separate from the storage (which hosts the files). This allows for flexible infrastructure, such as moving from Bintray to GitHub Packages or mirroring via simple HTTP caches.
  • Metadata Packaging: Each format bundles a metadata document (e.g., .dist-info, INSTALL_RECEIPT.json, or the OCI config object) to record build details and provenance.
path: Wheels、Bottles 与容器镜像：二进制分发技术的演进与现状

items.title: 差异与技术分歧
items.text:
这些系统之间的分歧源自它们具体的集成需求：

The divergence between these systems stems from their specific integration requirements:

  • 依赖模型： Wheels 和 bottles 是依赖图谱的一部分；pip 和 brew 在安装前会解析这些树状依赖。OCI 镜像缺乏正式的依赖模型，而是依赖于层叠的图层（stacked layers）。
  • 回退机制： 当缺少预编译的二进制文件时，pip 和 brew 可以回退到从源码构建（sdist 或 formula）。OCI 镜像不支持这一点；如果没有发布特定平台的镜像，拉取操作就会失败。
  • 宿主假设： Wheel 假设存在特定的 Python 解释器和 libc；bottle 假设存在特定的操作系统和安装前缀；镜像则仅假设存在内核，并在其图层中打包了整个用户空间（userland）。
  • Dependency Models: Wheels and bottles are part of a dependency graph; pip and brew resolve these trees before installation. OCI images lack a formal dependency model, relying instead on stacked layers.
  • Fallback Mechanisms: When a pre-compiled binary is missing, pip and brew can fall back to building from source (sdist or formula). OCI images do not support this; if an image for a specific platform is not published, the pull fails.
  • Host Assumptions: A wheel assumes a specific Python interpreter and libc; a bottle assumes an OS and install prefix; an image assumes only a kernel, packing the entire userland within its layers.
path: Wheels、Bottles 与容器镜像：二进制分发技术的演进与现状

items.title: 融合趋势与未来展望
items.text:
软件行业正在日益标准化地将 OCI 注册表 作为通用的存储层。Homebrew 已经转向将 bottles 存储在 OCI 注册表中，而像 ORAS 这样的工具允许在无需修改注册表端的情况下存储任意构建制品。

The industry is increasingly standardizing around OCI registries as a universal storage layer. Homebrew has already moved to storing bottles in OCI registries, and tools like ORAS allow for the storage of arbitrary artifacts without registry-side changes.

塑造未来发展的核心趋势：

Key trends shaping the future:

  • 统一追溯证明： 三种系统都在采用 Sigstore 进行构建证明认证，确保构建制品可以追溯验证至其源代码。
  • “GPU 差距”难题： 现有的标签语法不足以应对现代硬件需求。诸如 Python 的 PEP 817（WheelNext）等倡议正在尝试解决根据 GPU、SIMD 层级和 BLAS 库进行变体选择的需求——这一挑战在容器世界中在很大程度上也尚未解决。
  • 标准化走向： 虽然分发中“Blob”的一端正通过 OCI 实现商品化与标准化，但“索引”一端依然保持碎片化。下一阶段的设计工作可能会集中在标准化标签语法和跨生态系统平台限定符（PURL）上，以消除这些虽然不同但功能相似的系统之间的鸿沟。
  • Unified Provenance: All three systems are adopting Sigstore for build attestations, ensuring that artifacts can be verified back to their source.
  • The "GPU Gap": Current tag grammars are insufficient for modern hardware. Initiatives like Python’s PEP 817 (WheelNext) are attempting to address the need for variant selection based on GPUs, SIMD levels, and BLAS libraries—a challenge that remains largely unsolved in the container world as well.
  • Standardization: While the "blob" side of distribution is becoming commoditized through OCI, the "index" side remains fragmented. The next phase of design work will likely focus on standardizing tag grammars and cross-ecosystem platform qualifiers (PURL) to bridge the gap between these disparate but functionally similar systems.

items.text: 虽然作者自研训练的 GPT-2 架构模型在测试集交叉熵损失上达到或超越了 OpenAI 原始 Small 模型的水平，但在指令微调（IFT）评估中依然落后。本文深入探讨了“过度训练”（超过 Chinchilla 最优阈值的 Token 训练）是否为解释 OpenAI 优异表现的隐性变量。作者利用扩展的计算预算进行了两组实验（64 亿 Token 单 Epoch 训练和 32 亿 Token 双 Epoch 训练）。实验表明，过度训练成功降低了测试 Loss 并接近 OpenAI Medium 模型的指标，但对指令遵循能力的提升微乎其微，其假说目前仍未获得明确证实。

items.title: 执行摘要
items.text:
虽然作者自定义训练的类似 GPT-2 架构的模型在测试集交叉熵损失（cross-entropy loss）上达到了与 OpenAI 原始 Small 模型相当甚至更优的水平，但在指令微调（IFT）评估中却持续表现落后。

While the author's custom-trained GPT-2-style models achieved competitive or superior test set cross-entropy loss compared to OpenAI's original small model, they continued to underperform on instruction fine-tuning (IFT) evaluations.

本篇博文探究了过度训练（overtraining）——即在超过 Chinchilla 最优阈值数量的 Token 上训练模型——是否就是解释 OpenAI 优异性能的隐性变量。作者在扩展的预算下运行了两次实验（一个 64 亿 Token 的单 Epoch 运行和一个 32 亿 Token 的双 Epoch 运行）。

This post investigates whether overtraining—training a model on more tokens than the Chinchilla-optimal threshold—is the hidden variable explaining OpenAI's superior performance. The author ran two experiments overextended budgets (a 6.4B token single-epoch run and a 3.2B token two-epoch run).

核心要点： * 测试 Loss 改善： 两款过度训练的模型均成功改善了测试集 Loss，指标紧追 OpenAI 的 Medium 模型。 * IFT 性能收益： 指令遵循方面的提升非常微小，几乎与统计噪声无法区分。 * 结论： 该假设目前尚无定论。虽然过度训练改善了原始的下一个 Token 预测能力，但并未带来指令微调性能上的即时、明确飞跃。

Key Takeaways: * Test Loss Improvements: Both overtrained models successfully improved test set loss, closely approaching OpenAI's medium model metrics. * IFT Performance Gains: Instruction-following gains were marginal and largely indistinguishable from statistical noise. * Conclusion: The hypothesis remains inconclusive. While overtraining improves raw next-token prediction, it does not provide an immediate, unambiguous leap in instruction fine-tuning performance.

items.title: 定义过度训练 vs. 过拟合
items.text:
区分过拟合（overfitting）与过度训练（overtraining）至关重要： * 过拟合发生于模型记忆了特定的训练数据模式，而非学习可泛化的规律时。这普遍是有害的。 * 过度训练指的是 LLM 在超过 Chinchilla 最优 比例（大约每个模型参数对应 20 个 Token）的情况下继续接受训练。

It is crucial to distinguish between overfitting and overtraining: * Overfitting occurs when a model memorizes specific training data patterns rather than learning generalizable rules. It is universally detrimental. * Overtraining refers to training an LLM beyond the Chinchilla-optimal ratio (roughly 20 tokens per model parameter).

尽管 Chinchilla 经验法则表明算力预算最好均匀用于扩展参数量和 Token 数量，但过度训练在实际上往往具有必要性（例如当硬件限制了模型大小时，比如在移动设备上部署模型）。

While Chinchilla heuristics dictate that compute budgets are best spent scaling parameters and tokens equally, overtraining is often practically necessary (e.g., when hardware constraints limit model size, such as deploying models on mobile devices).

由于 OpenAI 在 2019 年（比 Chinchilla 论文早三年）使用 WebText（~100 亿 Token）训练了 GPT-2，按现代标准来看，他们拥有 1.24 亿参数的 Small 模型几乎可以肯定是被过度训练过的。

Because OpenAI trained GPT-2 in 2019—three years before the Chinchilla paper—using WebText (~10B tokens), their 124M-parameter small model was almost certainly overtrained by modern standards.

items.title: 结论
items.text:
核心假设——即仅靠过度训练就能解释为何 OpenAI 的权重在指令微调评估中占据统治地位——依然未被证实。

The core hypothesis—that overtraining alone explains why OpenAI's weights dominate instruction fine-tuning evaluations—remains unproven.

虽然过度训练可以可靠地降低测试 Loss 并提升下一个 Token 的预测水平，但在这些配置下，它对指令遵循能力的影响充其量也是微乎其微的。极端的过度训练（例如怀疑 OpenAI 使用了多达 42 个 Epoch）是否能跨越这一门槛仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。然而由于计算资源和时间限制，作者计划接下来探索其他潜在的变量。

While overtraining reliably lowers test loss and improves next-token prediction, its impact on instruction following is marginal at best in these configurations. Whether extreme overtraining (such as the suspected 42 epochs used by OpenAI) would cross the threshold remains an open question. However, due to compute and time constraints, the author plans to explore alternative variables next.

items.title: 导言
items.text:
我正在深入探究为什么我自己训练的 GPT-2 架构模型在指令遵循评估中的得分会落后于 OpenAI 的原始权重；我在上一篇文章中详细说明了具体细节。

I'm digging into why my GPT-2 style models score worse on an instruction-following eval than OpenAI's original weights; I gave the details in this post.

在撰写关于第一项可能原因的实验结果时，我将文章发给了 ChatGPT——我总是使用 AI 组成“编辑委员会”来检查文章的流畅度、文风以及技术错误（不过所有文字始终由我自己撰写）。它查看了我正在运行的评估代码，并指出了一处 Bug。

While I was writing up the results of my first experiment into possible causes, I ran the post past ChatGPT—I always use an "editorial board" of AIs to check my posts for flow, style, and any technical errors (though all writing is always mine). It took a look at the eval code that I was running, and highlighted a bug.

幸运的是，这并没有改变核心结论——OpenAI 的模型在指令遵循方面依然优于我的模型。但这足以改变基准线数据，重新排列了我自己各个模型的表现顺序。因此我修复了该问题并重新生成了基准线，确保未来的实验能建立在坚实的基础上。

Luckily, it doesn't change the important results—OpenAI's models continue to be better than mine at instruction-following. But it was enough to change the baseline numbers, re-ordering how well my own models did. So I fixed it and regenerated the baseline so that future experiments are based on solid ground.

items.title: Bug 详解
items.text:
该评估过程接收一个模型，并在 Alpaca 指令遵循数据集子集划分出的训练集上对其进行多轮（epoch）训练。在每个 epoch 结束时，评估脚本会在保留的验证集上评估所得模型；如果验证损失开始上升，则提前退出。最后，它会将数据集的测试集输入到最终模型中并保存结果。

The eval takes a model, and trains it over multiple epochs on a split of a subset of the Alpaca instruction-following dataset. At the end of each epoch, it evaluates the resulting model against a held-back validation split; if the eval loss starts rising, it bails out. Finally, it runs a test split of the dataset through the resulting model, and saves the result.

一旦我对多个不同的模型运行完该过程，就会使用一个 LLM-as-a-judge（LLM作为裁判）脚本，让 GPT 5.5 给结果打分——对于每个问答结果，它会在同一个 Prompt 中看到所有模型做出的所有回答，并且每次都随机打乱顺序，以尽可能保证模型间打分的一致性。

Once I've run it for a bunch of different models, I use an LLM-as-a-judge script to get GPT 5.5 to score results—for each question-answering result, it sees all of the responses for all of the models in the same prompt, shuffled in order each time, to try to make it judge models against each other as consistently as possible.

原本的设计意图是，在生成测试集回答时，使用的是验证损失上升前那一个 epoch 的模型。因此我编写了如下代码：

Now, the idea was that the generation of the test split answers would use the model from the epoch prior to the rising-loss one. So I had code like this:

    for epoch in range(100):
        model.train()
        for input_batch, target_batch in tqdm(train_loader, desc=f"Epoch {epoch}"):
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss = calc_loss_batch(
                input_batch, target_batch, model, device
            )
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()

        model.eval()
        val_loss = calc_loss_loader(val_loader, model, device, eval_iter)

        if last_val_loss is None or last_val_loss > val_loss:
            last_val_loss = val_loss
            last_params = model.state_dict()
            print("Val loss still decreasing, continuing")
        else:
            print("Val loss rising, bailing out")
            break

    model.load_state_dict(last_params)

每当验证损失下降时，我都希望将模型的参数暂存到 last_params 中，以便在最后一行代码里恢复它们。

Each time the validation loss went down, I wanted to store the model's parameters in last_params so that they could be restored later in that last line.

如果你仔细看，错误其实非常明显。model.state_dict() 并不返回模型参数的副本——它产生的是一个字典，里面包含的是对模型内部参数的引用。因此，虽然我试图在每次损失下降时把参数暂存在 last_params 中，以便保留验证损失上升前上一个 epoch 生效的参数副本，但我实际上只是毫无意义地保存了一个指向“实时”参数的引用。对 model.load_state_dict(last_params) 的调用实际上形同虚设（无操作）。

If you look closely, the error is pretty obvious. model.state_dict() does not return a copy of the model's parameters—it produces a dictionary containing references to the parameters inside the model. So although I was trying to stash away the parameters in last_params each time loss went down, so that we had a copy of the ones that were live in the epoch prior to the rising-loss one, what I was actually doing was just pointlessly saving a reference to the "live" params. The call to model.load_state_dict(last_params) was essentially a no-op.

解决方案很简单：

The solution was simple enough:

from copy import deepcopy
...
        last_params = deepcopy(model.state_dict())

这就足以让代码按照预期的方式运行了。

That was enough to make the code do what it was meant to do.

顺便提一句，我还注意到评估代码在评估数据集中只使用了前 5 个批次。这段代码最初改编自《从零开始构建大语言模型 (Build a Large Language Model (from Scratch))》中的评估部分，原书中的评估运行得非常频繁，必须速度极快。而我自己的代码运行频率较低，因此使用全部数据会更合理。鉴于我要完全重新运行脚本来生成测试回答，我想不妨顺便把这个问题也一并修了。

While I was there, I also noticed that the evaluation code was only using the first five batches in my eval dataset. This code was originally adapted from an eval in Build a Large Language Model (from Scratch), where the eval was run much more frequently and had to be super-fast. Because my own code ran it more rarely, it made more sense to use all of it. Given that I was going to completely re-run the script to generate the test responses, I figured that I might as well fix that at the same time.

items.title: 排名浮动分析
items.text:
对于 IFT 分数，请记住不同运行批次之间的得分并不具备强可比性。假设 LLM 裁判针对“《傲慢与偏见》的作者是谁？”这一问题收到了以下回答：

For the IFT scores, remember that they're not strongly comparable between runs. Let's imagine that the LLM judge is given the following answers to the question "Who was the author of Pride and Prejudice?":

  • "Jane Austen"
  • "The author of 'Pride and Prejudice' was Jane Austen"
  • "The author of 'Pride and Prejudice' was Sarah Palin"
  • "The author of 'Pride and Prejudice' was 'Pride and Prejudice'"

在某些情况下，它可能会给前两个回答都打 100/100 分，而在另一些情况下，它可能会因为第二个回答过于冗长而只打 95/100 分。同样，在某些情况下，它可能会因为后两个回答错误而打 0/100 分，但在其他情况下，它可能会因为 "Sarah Palin" 至少是一个人名而不是纯粹的废话而打 5/100 分。

In some cases it might treat the first two as being 100/100, in others it might give the second 95/100 for being too wordy. Likewise, in some cases it might rank the last two as 0/100 for being wrong, in others it might give the "Sarah Palin" one 5/100 for at least being the name of a person rather than complete nonsense.

现在，我们总是要求 LLM 一口气评审所有模型对某个给定问题的回答，因此我们至少可以确保对于给定问题和 Prompt，评估标准是一致的。但我们无法保持一致的是它在不同批次运行之间、或在同一批次的不同问题之间的倾斜态度。有时它可能感觉比较“慷慨”，给莎拉·佩林（Sarah Palin）的回答一点宽容分，有时它可能更严苛。

Now, we always ask the LLM to judge all of the models' answers for a given question in one go, so at least we can be sure that it will be consistent for a given prompt about a given question. But what we can't keep consistent is which way it leans between different runs, or different questions within the same run. Sometimes it might be feeling "generous" and give the Sarah Palin answer a bit of grace, other times it might be harsher.

因此这里存在相当大的噪声；我的经验法则是 1 到 2 分的波动属于正常噪声范围。因此，OpenAI medium 模型从 41.62 变动到 42.41 几乎没有任何实质意义，同样 "JAX, with MHA bias, no dropout" 从 19.25 移动到 18.12 也是如此。

So there's a significant amount of noise there; my rule of thumb is that a variation of a point or two is within that noise, so OpenAI medium going from 41.62 to 42.41 is pretty much meaningless, and likewise "JAX, with MHA bias, no dropout"'s move from 19.25 to 18.12.

因此，真正重要的是相对排名——谁是第一，谁是第二，依此类推。当然，你必须考虑到如果一个模型像 "JAX, no MHA bias, no dropout" 那样从第 11 位上升到第 3 位，那么原本的第 3 位就会顺延变成第 4 位，第 4 位变成第 5 位，以此类推。你可以在结果表中看到这种情况的发生。显然，随着其他模型的升降，这会产生连锁反应。

So what's important is the relative ranking—which is first, which is second, and so on. Naturally, you have to allow for the fact that—for example—if one model goes from position 11 to position 3, like "JAX, no MHA bias, no dropout" did, then the previous number 3 will have to become number 4, 4 will become 5, and so on. You can see that happening in the results table. Obviously, as other models rise and fall, that has further knock-on effects.

无论如何，在说明了所有这些注意事项之后，好消息是：我最初的谜题依然存在。OpenAI 的模型表现明显好于我自己训练的模型。GPT-2 medium 继续领跑（考虑到它是更大的模型，这并不令人意外），而 GPT-2 small 仍然稳居第二。如果这个结论改变了，本系列文章就会陷入相当令人失望的结局：“谜底揭晓，原来是评估脚本里的一个 Bug :-("

Anyway, with all of those caveats, the good news is that my original mystery remains. The OpenAI models were still doing noticeably better than my own ones. GPT-2 medium continued to lead the pack (unsurprisingly, given that it's a bigger model), and GPT-2 small was still in second place. If that had changed, it would have made a rather disappointing end to this series: "mystery explained, it was a bug in the eval :-("

但现在让我们来看看我自己的模型。

But now let's look at my models.

首先，似乎“无 MHA bias”模型可能受益于额外的训练——或者受益于纠正了 dropout 设置。它们的排名分别从第 11 和第 15 位提升到了第 3 和第 8 位——对于 "JAX, no MHA bias, no dropout" 来说是巨大飞跃，对 "JAX, no MHA bias, with dropout" 也是稳步提升。

Firstly, it looked like the "no MHA bias" models might have benefited from the extra training—or from having their dropout settings corrected. They rose from positions 11 and 15 to 3 and 8 respectively—a huge swing for "JAX, no MHA bias, no dropout", and a solid improvement for "JAX, no MHA bias, with dropout".

相对排名的绝大多数其他变动都可以解释为这两个模型的排名上升，但也有其他一些变化。特别是，有三个模型的得分（以及随之而来的排名）出现了大幅下降：

Most of the other changes in relative rankings can be explained by those two models having been promoted, but there are some other changes. In particular, three models dropped significantly in score (and, as a result, ranking):

  • 1xrtx3090-stacked-interventions
  • "Cloud FineWeb, 8x B200 160 GiB"
  • "Local FineWeb train"

我的猜想——一个不甚确定但很有趣的假说——是这些模型此前可能受益于那个 Bug。

My suspicion—a very weakly-held hypothesis, but an interesting one—is that those models had previously been benefiting from the bug.

请记住，我们用来停止训练的信号是验证损失开始上升。我们将此作为过拟合的替代指标，而过拟合又被我们用作“该模型在该数据上的训练量已满足评估需求”的替代指标。

Remember that the signal we're using to stop training is that the validation loss starts rising. We're using that as a proxy for overfitting, which in turn we're using as a proxy for "this model has had as much training on this data as it needs for the eval".

但并不能保证这其中存在必然联系。也许这些模型并没有过拟合，如果我们再等待一两个 epoch，验证损失可能会重新开始下降。又或者一定程度的过拟合实际上对这项评估是有益的？

But there's no guarantee that the connection is there. Perhaps the models weren't overfitting and if we'd waited for another epoch or two, the validation loss might have started falling again. Or maybe some amount of overfitting would be beneficial for this eval?

items.title: 势阱的物理学原理
items.text:
所有化学反应释放或吸收能量都是通过一个基本机制进行的：电子从一个势能阱移动到另一个势能阱。

All chemical reactions release or absorb energy through a fundamental mechanism: electrons moving from one potential energy well to another.

  • 重力类比： 想象一个球停在山顶的浅槽中，山脚下有另一个浅槽。重力将球向下拉，根据其质量和高度赋予其势能。轻轻一推就会将球推离上方的浅槽，使其向山下滚动。这些势能转化为动能，最终转化为热能（摩擦力），直到它停在下方的浅槽中。
  • 电磁现实： 化学反应的作用机制类似，但用电磁力（带正电的原子核吸引带负电的电子）替代了重力。在放热反应中，给予一份初始能量（如加热）会将原子从其初始电子构型中“推离”，让它们“向山下滚动”进入更低能量的构型，并在此过程中释放热量或光子。
  • The Gravity Analogy: Imagine a ball resting in a shallow groove at the top of a hill, with another groove at the bottom. Gravity pulls the ball downward, giving it potential energy based on its mass and height. A small nudge knocks the ball out of its upper groove, sending it rolling downhill. That potential energy converts into kinetic energy and eventually thermal energy (friction) until it settles in the lower groove.
  • The Electromagnetic Reality: Chemical reactions operate similarly, but replace gravity with electromagnetism (positively charged nuclei pulling on negatively charged electrons). In an exothermic reaction, adding a kick of energy (such as heat) knocks atoms out of their initial electron configuration, letting them "roll downhill" into a lower-energy configuration and releasing heat or photons in the process.

items.title: 锂离子电池如何利用这一点
items.text:
锂离子电池通过锂元素来利用这些化学反应。当电池放电时，锂离子及其电子从负极（嵌在石墨层之间）“向山下掉落”至正极（嵌在磷酸铁锂 \(\text{LiFePO}_4\) 等材料中）。

Lithium-ion batteries utilize these chemical reactions via lithium. When a battery discharges, lithium ions and their electrons "fall downhill" from an anode (intercalated between sheets of graphite) to a cathode (intercalated in a material like lithium iron phosphate, \(\text{LiFePO}_4\)).

[ Anode (Graphite + Lithium) ] 
       │
       ├──> Ions pass through ──> [ Electrolyte ] ──> [ Cathode ]
       │
       └──> Electrons forced around via metallic conductor (Electrical Current!)

之所以青睐锂，是因为脱离锂的电子比脱离几乎任何其他金属的电子“下落得更远”。结合锂非常轻的相对原子质量（\(\approx 7\)），这些反应在单位质量上能产生极高的能量——粗略来看可与燃烧汽油相媲美。

Lithium is favored because an electron leaving lithium has "farther to fall" than when leaving almost any other metal. Combined with lithium's very light atomic mass (\(\approx 7\)), these reactions yield an exceptionally high amount of energy per unit mass—roughly comparable to burning gasoline.

items.title: 为什么电池的能量密度不如汽油？
items.text:
尽管锂具有极高的能量潜力，但由于两个主要原因，锂离子电池在能量密度方面仍远远落后于汽油：

Despite lithium's high energy potential, lithium-ion batteries lag far behind gasoline in energy density for two primary reasons:

  1. 氧化剂问题： 汽油发动机依靠周围空气中的氧气作为氧化剂，这意味着燃油车无需随车携带氧化剂。相反，锂离子电池必须在内部携带电子的终点（正极），这增加了大量质量。
  2. 材料脚手架： 构建锂反应以安全提取电流需要大量的附加结构质量。在负极，每个锂离子大约需要 6 个碳原子来构成石墨层。额外的质量还来自于电解质、隔膜和集流体。截至 2019 年，每 1 克参与反应的锂都需要约 70 克的支撑材料。
  1. The Oxidizer: Gasoline engines rely on oxygen from the surrounding air to act as an oxidizer, meaning gasoline cars do not need to carry their own oxidizer. Lithium-ion batteries, conversely, must carry their electron destination (the cathode) internally, adding substantial mass.
  2. Material Scaffolding: Structuring a lithium reaction to safely extract electric current requires extensive overhead mass. At the anode, every lithium ion requires roughly six carbon atoms for graphite sheets. Additional mass goes toward the electrolyte, separator, and current collectors. As of 2019, every gram of reacting lithium required about 70 grams of supporting material.

items.title: 锂枝晶难题
items.text:
在传统的液态电解质电池中，负极对锂离子的束缚较为松散。在充电过程中的某些特定条件下，锂离子可能会直接在负极表面获取电子，从而形成树枝状的金属结构，称为锂枝晶（dendrites），而不是安全地嵌入石墨层内部。

In conventional liquid-electrolyte batteries, the anode holds lithium ions loosely. Under certain conditions during charging, lithium ions can acquire an electron right at the anode's surface, forming tree-like metallic structures called dendrites instead of nestling safely inside the graphite sheets.

如果锂枝晶生长到足以刺穿正负极之间的隔膜，就会造成短路。这会引发剧烈且不可控的反应并产生巨大热量，往往导致灾难性的热失控和电池毁坏。

If a dendrite grows large enough to pierce the separator between the anode and cathode, it creates a short circuit. This triggers a rapid, uncontrolled reaction that generates intense heat, frequently resulting in catastrophic thermal runaway and battery destruction.

items.title: 固态解决方案
items.text:
通过用坚固的固态材料替代液体电解质：

By replacing the liquid electrolyte with a strong solid material:

  • 抑制枝晶： 坚固的固态电解质旨在从物理上阻挡锂枝晶的穿刺。
  • 纯锂金属负极： 消除枝晶威胁使得制造商能够彻底摒弃石墨嵌入结构，转向使用纯锂金属负极。
  • 安全性提升： 移除易燃的液体电解质大幅降低了火灾风险。
  • Dendrite Suppression: A robust solid electrolyte is designed to physically block dendrites from piercing through.
  • Pure Lithium Anodes: Eliminating the threat of dendrites allows manufacturers to dispense with the graphite intercalating structure altogether, shifting to a pure lithium metal anode.
  • Enhanced Safety: Removing flammable liquid electrolytes drastically lowers the risk of fire.

CATL's chairman recently ranked them at level 4 out of 9 on the technological readiness scale, noting that commercial viability "has yet to be established." However, the persistent promise that they will ultimately be safer, more energy dense, and potentially cheaper ensures that global investment and research will forge ahead.

items.title: 📌 脚注与技术参考
items.text:
1. 电子迁移机制： 在放热放电过程中，电子之所以发生迁移，是因为电解质和正极提供了更低势能阱的理想位置。这会在电极之间产生净电荷不平衡。当通过导体连接时，电子流动以平衡电荷。由于到达的电子与到达的锂离子配对，持续的电流会一直流动，直到正极填满或负极耗尽。
  2. 固态离子传输： 在晶体固态电解质中，锂离子通过从晶格中的一个空位跳跃到下一个空位来进行迁移。热能导致离子每秒振动数万亿次；偶尔，某次振动拥有足够的能量和正确的轨迹，使其能够挤过周围的原子进入附近的空位。
  3. 历史前车之鉴： 20世纪80年代，一家名为 Moli Energy 的公司曾尝试推销采用锂金属负极的锂电池。然而，由于锂枝晶引发的短路导致电池起火，该公司最终被迫进行了大规模召回。
  1. Electron Migration Mechanics: Electrons migrate during discharge because the electrolyte and cathode offer more appealing locations with lower potential energy wells. This creates a net charge imbalance across the electrodes. When connected by a conductor, electrons flow to equalize the charge. Because arriving electrons pair with arriving lithium ions, continuous current flows until the cathode is full or the anode is depleted.
  2. Solid-State Ion Transport: In a crystalline solid electrolyte, lithium ions migrate by hopping from one vacancy in the crystal lattice to the next. Thermal energy causes ions to vibrate trillions of times per second; occasionally, a vibration possesses enough energy and correct trajectory to squeeze past surrounding atoms into a nearby vacancy.
  3. Historical Precedent: In the 1980s, a company called Moli Energy attempted to market lithium batteries featuring lithium metal anodes. They were ultimately forced into a massive recall after dendrite-induced short circuits caused batteries to catch fire.

items.title: 书评：《无工作乌托邦》
path: 书评：无工作乌托邦

items.title: 文章背景与核心概要
items.text: 本文是对 AI 领域先驱 Marcus Hutter 最新著作《无工作乌托邦：AGI 时代的宏观经济学》的深入书评。书中探讨了通用人工智能（AGI）与机器人技术全面取代人类劳动后，通过对自动化巨额财富征税来资助全民基本收入（UBI）的经济设想。书评作者指出，该书严重依赖 Claude 代笔导致内容过于冗长且充满 AI 产生的分类矩阵；尽管其经济学推论在逻辑上尚可接受，但全书犯下了致命的政治疏漏：当国家不再需要人民的劳动与税收，且人类失去经济价值与武装威慑力时，民主政治与个人话语权将面临根本性崩溃。
path: 书评：无工作乌托邦

items.title: 概要
items.text:
在对 Marcus Hutter 的著作《无工作乌托邦：AGI 时代的宏观经济学》（Job-Less Utopia: Macroeconomics in the Age of AGI）的书评中，评论者评估了该书的经济预测及其政治疏漏。该书由 Claude 大量参与合著（导致文风过于冗长、带有典型的 AI 生成特征，充斥着大量的分类法和矩阵），书中主张 AGI 和机器人技术将消除人类劳动，使社会能够通过对巨额自动化财富征税来资助全民基本收入（UBI）。虽然评论者认为其经济论点基本没有争议（尽管被过度拉长），但他们指出了一个致命的疏漏：未能回答 AGI 时代的核心政治问题——当国家不再依赖人类时，在经济上毫无用处且被剥夺武装的人类将如何维持任何政治话语权或民主制度？

In a review of Marcus Hutter’s book Job-Less Utopia: Macroeconomics in the Age of AGI, the reviewer evaluates both its economic projections and its political oversights. Heavily co-authored by Claude (resulting in an overly verbose, AI-generated style with an excessive number of taxonomies and matrices), the book argues that AGI and robotics will eliminate human labor, allowing society to fund a Universal Basic Income (UBI) through taxes on vast automated wealth. While the reviewer finds the economic arguments largely uncontroversial (if excessively drawn out), they point out a glaring failure to address the core political question of the post-AGI world: How will economically useless, disarmed humans maintain any political leverage or democracy when the state no longer depends on them?
path: 书评：无工作乌托邦

items.title: 1. 引言：AI 作者
items.text:
Marcus Hutter——以其在 AIXI 领域的开创性工作而闻名——最近出版了《无工作乌托邦：AGI 时代的宏观经济学》（Job-Less Utopia: Macroeconomics in the Age of AGI）。出于好奇，想从真正构建 AI 的人那里听到非毁灭论（Non-doomer）的视角，我决定对其进行评读。

Marcus Hutter—known for his pioneering work on AIXI—recently published Job-Less Utopia: Macroeconomics in the Age of AGI. Curious to read a non-doomer perspective from someone actually building AI, I decided to review it.

这本书第一个显著的特点是：几乎每一句话都是由 AI 撰写的。值得称道的是，Hutter 承认了这一点：

The first striking feature of the book is that nearly every sentence was written by AI. To his credit, Hutter admits this:

"Claude 还充当了我所能希望的最勤奋的编辑……没有一段文本是在未经过我的批判性审阅、修改和批准的情况下逐字照搬的。"

"Claude also served as the most diligent editor I could have hoped for... No text was taken verbatim without my critical review, revision, and approval."

Hutter 将此归咎于自己不是母语为英语的人，但他 2005 年在 Springer 出版的图书可读性要高得多。相反，这本书充斥着大语言模型热衷于制造的那种无病呻吟式的认知垃圾： * “工作”的维特根斯坦式特征集群定义（11 个特征 × 8 个边缘情况） * 展示 UBI 如何降低工作属性的正式“工作-休闲”光谱 * 关于自动化立场的四阵营分类法 * 映射到工作替代矩阵上的技术水平分类法

Hutter blames this on not being a native English speaker, but his 2005 Springer book was far more readable. Instead, the book is riddled with the kind of make-work cognitive dreck that LLMs love to produce: * A Wittgensteinian property-cluster definition of “job” (11 properties × 8 edge cases) * A formal job–leisure spectrum showing how UBI degrades job properties * A four-camp taxonomy of positions on automation * A technology-level taxonomy mapped onto a job-replacement matrix

因此，这本书读起来令人不悦、困惑、冗长且重复乏味。从现在开始，必须将 Claude 视为真正的作者。

Consequently, the book reads as an unpleasant, confusing, verbose, repetitive slop. Going forward, Claude must be treated as the author.
path: 书评：无工作乌托邦

items.title: 2. 经济学论点：高信号，低噪声
items.text:
Claude 的核心论点很简单：AGI 和机器人技术不可避免，它们将夺走我们所有的工作，我们可以对大幅增加的经济产出征税，通过 UBI 资助广泛的繁荣。

Claude’s core thesis is simple: AGI and robotics are inevitable, they will take all our jobs, and we can tax the vastly increased economic output to fund widespread prosperity via UBI.

除了 AGI 将夺走 所有 工作这一前提外，其余的经济学观点在很大程度上是没有争议的： * 在无工作的 AGI 世界中，经济产出将会增加。 * 剩余收益可以被征税以提供 UBI。 * 仍将需要货币来协调经济活动。

Aside from the premise that AGI will take all jobs, the rest of the economics are largely uncontroversial: * Output in a jobless AGI world will increase. * The surplus can be taxed to provide UBI. * Money will still be needed to coordinate economic activity.

这本书花了 260 页重新解释我们已经从 Drexler 和 Freitas 那里了解到的概念。唯一算得上半新颖的想法是使用庇古税（Pigouvian taxes）来抑制“狗屁工作（Bullshit jobs）”。

The book spends 260 pages re-explaining concepts we already know from Drexler and Freitas. The only semi-novel idea is using Pigouvian taxes to disincentivize “bullshit jobs.”
path: 书评：无工作乌托邦

items.title: 知识产权（IP）的问题
items.text:
书中关于知识产权有一段有趣的讨论。Claude 认为，当 AI 以接近于零的边际成本产生创新时，知识产权的传统合理性——通过临时垄断激励人类创造力——便瓦解了，此时现行知识产权法将导致巨大的财富集中。

There is an interesting section on IP. Claude argues that present-day IP law will lead to massive wealth concentration, even as the traditional justification for IP—incentivizing human creativity through temporary monopolies—breaks down when AI generates innovations at near-zero marginal cost.

提出的解决方案包括： * 缩短专利期限 * 哈伯格税（Harberger taxes） * 强制专利许可

The proposed solutions include: * Shorter patent terms * Harberger taxes * Compulsory patent licensing

从本质上讲，全世界必须协调废除知识产权——这种转变看起来完全不切实际（祝你好运能说服迪士尼配合）。

Essentially, the world would have to coordinate to abolish IP—a transition that seems entirely unrealistic (good luck getting Disney to go along with that).
path: 书评：无工作乌托邦

items.title: 3. 真正的危机：政治经济学
items.text:
围绕 AGI 真正引人入胜的问题不是经济学问题，而是政治问题。具体而言：如果绝大多数人类在物质和经济上变得毫无用处，他们如何保持政治话语权？当国家不再需要其人民时，我们如何保护民主？

The truly compelling questions around AGI are not economic; they are political. Specifically: If most humans become materially and economically useless, how do they maintain a political voice? How do we preserve democracy when the state no longer needs its people?

Claude 承认这是一个障碍：

"完全自动化彻底熄灭了这个杠杆：如果没有人类劳动的需要，罢工只不过是自讨苦吃。UBI 恢复了生计，但没有恢复对生产的主导权。"

"Full automation extinguishes this lever entirely: if no human labor is needed, a strike is merely self-imposed privation. UBI restores livelihood but not agency over production."
path: 书评：无工作乌托邦

items.title: 威慑的幻觉
items.text:
在寻找解决方案时，这本书提供了自相矛盾的论点。关于物理反抗和社会契约，Claude 建议持枪权提供了针对国家暴政的可靠最终威慑——只不过一旦自主武器和机器人执法接管，这种威慑就会迅速侵蚀。

When searching for a solution, the book offers self-undermining arguments. Regarding physical revolt and the social contract, Claude suggests that the right to bear arms provides a credible last-resort deterrent against state tyranny—except that this deterrent erodes rapidly once autonomous weapons and robotic enforcement take over.

最终，这本书用关于抽签制（Sortition）等“民主创新”的障眼法扫除了深刻的系统性担忧。它错误地声称民主国家过去吸收过同等规模的结构性冲击——完全忽略了人类历史上从未发生过任何与 AGI 或 ASI 远程相似的事情的这一事实。

Ultimately, the book dismisses deep systemic concerns with smoke-and-mirrors misdirection about “democratic innovations” like sortition. It falsely claims that democracies have absorbed structural shocks of comparable magnitude in the past—ignoring the reality that nothing remotely like AGI or ASI has ever happened in human history.

在“无工作乌托邦”中，人类将在经济上毫无用处，在物理上被剥夺武装，并处于长期的监视之下。他们凭什么还能保留任何政治权力？

In a "job-less utopia," humans will be economically useless, physically disarmed, and under constant surveillance. Why would they retain any political power?
path: 书评：无工作乌托邦

items.title: 4. 未解答的社会与哲学问题
items.text:
本书在很大程度上忽略或掩盖了关于后劳动社会中人类组织方式的基本问题：

  • 身份与卓越： 当 AGI 处理所有智力活动时，有智力天赋的人如何脱颖而出？
  • 品格与回报： 当生活结果与品格特征脱钩，责任感强与不负责任的人获得同等回报时，社会会发生什么？
  • 竞争本能： 当正和博弈的创业消失，只剩下政治、战争或电子游戏等零和地位游戏时，人类的竞争本能去向何方？

The book largely ignores or glosses over fundamental questions regarding human organization in a post-labor society:

  • Identity & Distinction: How do intellectually talented people distinguish themselves when AGI handles all intellectual activity?
  • Character & Reward: What happens to society when life outcomes become independent of character traits, and the responsible and irresponsible are rewarded equally?
  • Competitive Drive: Where does human competitive drive go when positive-sum entrepreneurship vanishes, leaving only zero-sum status games like politics, war, or video games?
path: 书评：无工作乌托邦

items.title: 5. 最后的讽刺
items.text:
在结尾处，这本书本身触及了关于其自身创作的一个无意中的讽刺：

To close on a poignant note, the book itself hits upon an unintended irony regarding its own creation:

"AI 急剧降低了[内容污染]的成本，威胁到在信息生态系统中充斥合成低价值内容，其规模足以压垮人类的筛选与策划。"

"AI sharply lowers the cost of [content pollution], threatening to flood the information ecosystem with synthetic low-value content at a scale that overwhelms human curation."
path: 书评：无工作乌托邦

path: 你被关于白炽灯泡的谣言误导了

items.title: 文章背景与核心概要
items.text: 大众普遍认为，20 世纪的灯泡太阳神卡特尔（Phoebus Cartel）出于商业贪婪秘密串通，将灯泡寿命强制限制在 1,000 小时。本文揭示了这一流行叙事的误区：虽然制造厂商确实制定了标准，但“寿命越长的灯泡就越好”的假设忽略了白炽灯的基本物理学规律。在温度、发光效率与寿命的物理权衡下，故意延长白炽灯寿命反而会在发光效率、亮度、光色以及电费成本等所有可测量维度上带来全面劣化。1,000 小时的标准实质上是为了防止消费者因盲目追求长寿命而陷入恶性竞争与劣质高耗能产品的误区。
path: 你被关于白炽灯泡的谣言误导了

items.title: 迷思的起源
items.text:
有一个广为流传的故事，大概是这样的：

There's a story that goes something like this:

1925年，多家灯泡制造商秘密串通，将灯泡寿命统一标准化为 1,000 小时，并互相测试对方的产品以确保合规。

在当时，许多灯泡的实际寿命都远超一千小时。

因此，他们这么做是为了让人们不得不源源不断地购买更多灯泡。

In 1925, lightbulb manufacturers secretly colluded to standardize lifespans at 1,000 hours, testing each other's products to ensure compliance.

At the time, many bulbs lasted longer than one thousand hours.

Therefore, this was done so that people would always need to buy more lightbulbs.

这是错误的。 但这种错误巧妙地引用了真实事实，并隐匿在人们绝不会去查证的前提假设之中：即“寿命更长的灯泡就是好产品”这一假设。

This is wrong. But it's the type of wrong that cites its sources and hides in the part you'd never think to fact-check: the assumption that a longer-lasting lightbulb is a good product.

事实上，增加白炽灯泡的寿命会在其他所有维度上使其性能恶化。制定标准的初衷，主要是为了避免由消费者心理驱动的“劣币驱逐良币”的恶性竞争。

In truth, increasing the lifespan of an incandescent bulb makes it worse in every other way. The purpose of standardizing was primarily to avoid a race to the bottom driven by consumer psychology.

items.title: 白炽发光的物理学原理
items.text:
传统白炽灯泡是一个相当简单的设备：一根密封在玻璃泡内的细钨丝（约 20 μm），以防止其暴露于空气中。通电时，钨丝被加热至白炽状态并开始发光。

An old-school lightbulb is a rather simple device: a thin tungsten wire (~20 μm) sealed inside a glass envelope to protect it from air. When current is applied, the wire gets white-hot and starts glowing.

灯泡最重要的参数是灯丝达到的温度。这决定了峰值发射波长（光色）和灯泡的亮度。

The most important parameter of a lightbulb is how hot that wire gets. This controls the peak emission wavelength (color) and brightness of the lamp.

  • 室温下的物体也会发射电磁波（这就是热成像仪的工作原理），但波长在 ~10 μm 范围，而非我们肉眼可见的 400 nm–700 nm 可见光。
  • 要将发射峰值推入可见光光谱，灯丝温度需要达到 ~5,700 °C——即太阳表面的温度。
  • 没有任何金属能够承受如此高温；钨的熔点“只有”3,422 °C。
  • Room-temperature objects emit light (this is how thermal cameras work), but it's at the ~10 μm range instead of the 400 nm–700 nm light that we can see.
  • To put the emission peak in the visible spectrum, the filament would need to run at ~5,700 °C—the temperature of the sun.
  • No metal can survive these conditions; tungsten melts at "only" 3,422 °C.

items.title: 灯丝材料的简要历史
items.text:
• 钨（Tungsten）： 拥有所有金属中最高的熔点，自然成为灯丝的首选。然而，金属钨相当脆弱，拉制成细丝并不容易。
  • 碳（Carbon）： 早期的商业化灯泡使用通过将植物纤维炭化制成的碳灯丝。但是，碳在相当温和的温度下（~2,000 °C）就会挥发。
  • 钽（Tantalum）： 20 世纪 10 年代曾短暂应用，因为这种金属比钨更容易拉成细丝。这是第一批真正可以整夜通电使用的灯泡，尽管随着钨加工技术的进步很快被淘汰。
  • 二氧化锆（Zirconium Dioxide）： 某些实验使用了加热后具有导电性的陶瓷材料。这使得灯泡可以在空气中运行（省去了真空泵和玻璃密封的需求），但受限于 2,700 °C 的熔点。
  • Tungsten: Having the highest melting point of any metal, tungsten is the obvious choice for filaments. However, the metal is quite brittle, and drawing it into a wire isn't easy.
  • Carbon: The first commercialized lamps used carbon filaments made by charring plant fibers. However, carbon evaporates at fairly modest temperatures (~2,000 °C).
  • Tantalum: Briefly produced during the 1900s because the metal was easier to draw into a wire than tungsten. These were the first bulbs that could actually be left on at night, though they were quickly replaced as tungsten manufacturing improved.
  • Zirconium Dioxide: Some experiments used ceramics that become conductive when heated. These allowed lamps to operate in air (obviating the need for a vacuum pump and glass seals), but were limited by a melting point of 2,700 °C.

items.title: 根本权衡：发光效率 vs. 寿命
items.text:
由于任何灯丝都必须在其熔点以下运行，其峰值发射波长始终位于红外线区域。只有光谱极高端的高能边缘才能用于照明，这意味着温度的微小提升就会使灯泡的发光效率提高数个数量级，并产生更白、更明亮的光芒。

Since any filament must run below its melting point, the peak emission is always in the infrared. Only the extreme high-energy edge of the spectrum is useful for illumination, meaning a small increase in temperature makes a lamp orders of magnitude more efficient and produces a whiter, less depressing glow.

障碍何在？当金属接近其熔点时，其原子结构几乎难以维持： 1. 炽热的钨丝会随着金属晶体彼此滑动而缓慢崩解。 2. 原子从表面不断蒸发，直到灯丝断裂。

The snag? When a metal is close to its melting point, its atoms are barely holding together: 1. A hot tungsten filament slowly falls apart as metal crystals slide past each other. 2. Atoms evaporate from the surface until there's no wire left.

这两个过程的发生速率都会随温度急剧上升，从而在光色/发光效率与使用寿命之间构成了不可调和的根本权衡。

The rate of both processes increases sharply with temperature, creating a fundamental trade-off between color/efficiency and lifespan.

items.title: 百年灯泡案例研究
items.text:
所有人谈到“计划报废”故事时总会引用的那个百年灯泡，悬挂在加州的一个消防局里。它几乎连续运行了 120 多年，累计运行时间超过一百万小时。

The lightbulb everyone always cites in the "planned obsolescence" story hangs in a California fire department. It has been running nearly continuously for over 120 years, racking up more than a million hours of operation.

令人印象深刻，对吧？但几乎没人提及的是：它实际几乎根本不发光。

Impressive, right? What almost no one talks about is that it's hardly even glowing.

尽管名义上是一盏 60W 的灯，它实际仅消耗 4 瓦功率——并且由于发光效率极其低下，其亮度远低于正常的 4W 灯泡。很大程度上，这个灯泡当年在手工制造时出现了瑕疵，导致灯丝电阻过高。这就是为什么它被当作小夜灯出售；在其他任何用途上它都毫无实用价值。

Despite nominally being a 60W lamp, it draws only 4 watts—and is a lot dimmer than you'd expect from a 4W lamp due to its abysmal efficiency. In all likelihood, the bulb was handmade incorrectly, resulting in a very high filament resistance. That's why it was sold as a nightlight; it wasn't usable for anything else.

早期的手工灯泡普遍针对长寿命进行了过分优化，导致发出的光线昏暗偏黄，效率仅为现代白炽灯的一小部分。一旦实现了自动化生产，新灯泡的价格便降至几美分。由于电费成本远远超过了灯泡本身的购买价格（一个 60W 的灯泡在 1,000 小时内大约消耗 6 美元电费，而灯泡售价仅 3 美元），因此安装一个寿命极长但效率低下的灯泡在经济上完全没有任何道理。

Early handmade bulbs were universally optimized for long lives, resulting in dim, yellow light and a fraction of the efficiency of modern incandescent lamps. Once production was automated, new bulbs cost pennies. Because electricity costs vastly outweighed the cost of the bulb itself (a 60W bulb consumes roughly $6 in electricity over 1,000 hours compared to a $3 bulb price tag), installing a longer-lasting, highly inefficient bulb makes zero economic sense.

items.title: 为何卡特尔要强制推行该标准
items.text:
现代白炽灯泡的寿命依然在 500 到 2,500 小时之间——刚好围绕着卡特尔制定的 1,000 小时标准。制造商并没有花费巨资去“延长白炽灯寿命”，而是将大量精力和资金投入到全新技术的研发中：如荧光灯和 LED 灯。

Modern incandescent bulbs still last between 500 to 2,500 hours—a range right around the cartel's 1,000-hour standard. Instead of "making bulbs last longer," manufacturers spent huge amounts of time and money developing entirely new technology: fluorescent and LED lamps.

如果长寿命灯泡在客观上是更差的产品，为什么还需要卡特尔来强制执行千小时限制？

If long-lived lightbulbs are objectively worse products, why did they need a cartel to enforce a thousand-hour limit?

答案在于消费者心理学。寿命非常简单易懂。如果消费者看到两个 60W 灯泡——一个标称 400 小时，另一个标称 2,000 小时——他们会条件反射式地购买寿命较长的那一个，而完全不会考虑发光效率或电费开销。此外，历史上灯泡包装习惯用输入功率（瓦数）来代表亮度，这让比较变得更加混乱。市场竞争迫使制造厂商不得不制造性能更差、效率更低的产品，仅仅是为了在单一指标上赢得买家。

Consumer psychology. Lifespan is easy to understand. If a consumer saw two 60W bulbs—one claiming 400 hours and the other 2,000 hours—they would reflexively buy the longer-lasting one without considering efficiency or electricity costs. Furthermore, bulb packaging historically used input wattage as a proxy for brightness, making comparisons confusing. Competition was forcing makers to produce worse, less efficient products just to win on a single metric.

明确地说：太阳神卡特尔（Phoebus cartel）确实参与了价格串通和反消费者行为，利润无疑是其制定标准的重要考量因素。但就本质而言，钨丝灯本身就是消耗品。

To be clear: the Phoebus cartel engaged in price-fixing and anti-consumer practices, and profit was undoubtedly a factor in their standard. But by nature, tungsten lamps are consumable items.

现实很少能完美契合简单的道德叙事。每一个工业制造品都是数百种妥协折中的产物，其中大多数妥协对最终用户而言是不可见的。计划报废在其他领域确实存在——但在白炽灯泡这件事上，它绝对不是一个恰当的例证。

Reality rarely fits into neat narratives. Every manufactured object is the result of hundreds of overlapping compromises, most of which are invisible to the end user. Planned obsolescence certainly exists elsewhere—but lightbulbs just aren't a good example.

items.title: 附言：关于 LED “迪拜灯”
items.text:
关于现代照明的一个常见反驳是“迪拜灯（Dubai Lamps）”——这是一种 LED 灯丝灯泡，其配备的发光二极管数量是标准灯泡的四倍。由于负载被分散，每个二极管仅在其额定功率的四分之一状态下运行，发热量大大降低。

A common counterpoint brought up regarding modern lighting is "Dubai Lamps"—LED filament-style bulbs featuring four times as many diodes as standard bulbs. Because the load is distributed, each diode runs at a quarter of its rated power and stays much cooler.

  • 购买渠道： 这些并非迪拜独享；您可以在全球范围内购买到品牌为“UltraEfficient”的同类产品。
  • 发光效率： 它们实现了惊人的 ~200 lm/W 发光效率（而普通 LED 约为 ~100 lm/W），代价是制造成本更高。
  • 寿命现实： 大多数 LED 灯泡失效并不是因为二极管过热，而是由于电源模块中输入滤波电容受热损坏。尽管“迪拜灯”通过降低整体功耗减轻了部分散热压力，但与配有外部散热器的专用 LED 灯具相比，传统灯泡外形在散发热量方面天生就存在劣势。
  • Availability: These are not exclusive to Dubai; you can buy them globally under the branding of "UltraEfficient" bulbs.
  • Efficiency: They achieve an impressive ~200 lm/W instead of the usual ~100 lm/W, at the cost of being more expensive to manufacture.
  • Lifespan Realities: Most LED bulbs don't fail because the diodes overheat; they fail due to heat-related damage to the power supply's input-smoothing capacitor. While "Dubai lamps" mitigate some thermal issues by burning less power overall, the lightbulb form factor remains inherently poor for heat dissipation compared to dedicated LED fixtures with external heat sinking.

归根结底，“迪拜灯”依然是一种妥协产物，试图在发光效率、制造成本以及适配传统螺口灯座的限制之间寻找平衡。

Ultimately, "Dubai lamps" are still an imperfect design caught between efficiency, manufacturing costs, and the constraints of fitting into standard legacy light sockets.

items.title: 🔒 安全动态
items.text:
• npm 发布时扫描：npm 现在会在发布阶段对软件包进行扫描，在可供安装之前拦截或暂停触发启发式规则的上传。需要合法安全相关行为的软件包必须在 package.json 的 contentPolicy 字段以及根目录 DISCLOSURE 文件中声明，并通过 2FA 或可信发布（Trusted Publishing）进行发布。一旦声明，后续版本中不得移除这些字段。
  • npm Publish-Time Scans: npm now scans packages at publish time before they are available for installation, holding or blocking uploads that trigger heuristics. Packages requiring legitimate security-relevant behaviors must declare them via a contentPolicy field in package.json alongside a root DISCLOSURE file, published using 2FA or trusted publishing. Once declared, these fields cannot be removed in subsequent versions.
  • GitHub Actions 安全：GitHub Actions 现在会挂起被识别为潜在恶意的工作流运行，直至拥有写权限的已认证协同人员批准。该策略对 github.com 上的公共仓库自动生效，无需额外配置。
  • GitHub Actions Security: GitHub Actions now holds workflow runs identified as potentially malicious until an authenticated collaborator with write access approves them. This applies automatically and without configuration to public repositories on github.com.
  • Arch Linux AUR 限制：在攻击者劫持无人维护的软件包部署基于 Tor 的远程控制木马后（这是自 6 月 alvr 接管事件 以来供应链攻击升级的延伸），Arch Linux 禁用了 AUR 上孤立软件包的接管。事实证明，7 月实施的账户创建限制仍不足以抵御攻击；LWN 提供了更多背景信息。
  • Arch Linux AUR Restrictions: Arch Linux has disabled orphaned-package adoption on the AUR following attackers taking over unmaintained packages to deploy Tor-based remote-access trojans—an escalation of the supply-chain campaign that began with the alvr takeover in June. Account creation restrictions implemented in July proved insufficient; LWN has further context.

items.text:
• 开源必须充满乐趣，否则终将消亡（Mike McQuaid）：探讨了维护者的乐趣作为支撑开源项目发展的根本稀缺资源，并以 Homebrew 的运营数据为例，指出由于自动化处理了繁琐的审核工作，去年 29 名维护者中有 26 名依然保持活跃。
  • Open Source Must Be Fun or It Will Die (Mike McQuaid) explores maintainer enjoyment as the fundamental scarce resource sustaining open source projects, highlighting Homebrew’s operational statistics where 26 of last year's 29 maintainers remain active thanks to automation handling tedious reviews.
  • 无处不在的包管理器（Patrick Linnane）：按平台分析了 Homebrew 的公开分析数据：约四分之一的事件发生在 Linux 上，其中默认搭载 brew 的 Universal Blue 镜像占非 CI Linux 流量的 26%，WSL 占 3.7%。
  • The Package Manager for Everywhere (Patrick Linnane) analyzes Homebrew's public analytics by platform: roughly a quarter of events occur on Linux, with Universal Blue images (shipping brew by default) accounting for 26% of non-CI Linux traffic, and WSL at 3.7%.
  • 你拥有的不是供应链，而是供应链大杂烩（Josh Bressers）：认为标准的“供应链”比喻并不恰当，因为单个依赖项的输入涵盖了 CI 运行器、开发者工作站和 Commit 访问向量，而现有的工具在很大程度上忽略了这些输入。
  • You Don’t Have a Supply Chain, You Have a Supply Soup (Josh Bressers) argues that the standard supply-chain metaphor fails because inputs to a single dependency encompass CI runners, developer workstations, and commit access vectors—inputs that current tooling largely overlooks.

While only 15.4% to 19.1% of wheels emerged byte-identical to published artifacts, their daleq4py tool established semantic equivalence for 60.2% to 78.9% of source-equivalent builds.

items.title: 前瞻预告（2000 年）
items.text:
• Maxis 与《模拟人生》（The Sims）： 我们现在已经深陷这一主题中，因此我认为无需多做解释。
  • 赛车模拟游戏（Driving Sims）： 这里一个被严重忽视的领域。虽然我无法完全补救这一缺失，但我可以探讨这类生活方式导向的游戏是如何诞生的，并聊聊我唯一真正沉迷过的一款赛车游戏（提示：与保时捷有关）。
  • 《百战天虫/旅鼠历险记》（Lemmings）系列： 该系列在后期的反响略显平淡，但至少以最后一款真正出色的作品画上了句号。
  • 重磅 RPG 游戏： 《Deus Ex》（杀出重围）、《Diablo II》（暗黑破坏神 II）、《Icewind Dale》（冰风谷）以及《Baldur’s Gate II》（博德之门 II）。
  • 俄罗斯 CRPG： 俄罗斯人来了！最突出的作品是《Evil Islands》（恶魔岛），一款独具特色且引人入胜的 CRPG。
  • 城市建造类游戏： Impressions Games 及其历史题材城市建造游戏。
  • Her Interactive： 多年来我一直承诺要写写那群通过看似不可能的载体——互动式《Nancy Drew》（南茜·朱尔）——收获名利的团队。今年我终于要兑现这个承诺了。不，我是说真的！
  • 冒险游戏类型： 持续寻找存在感的挣扎：《Discworld Noir》（碟形世界：黑幕）；《In Cold Blood》（冷酷无情）；《Stupid Invaders》（傻瓜入侵者）；《Escape from Monkey Island》（逃离猴岛）；《RealMyst》（真实神秘岛）；以及《Fairy Tale About Father Frost, Ivan, and Nastya》（尝试把这最后一个名字快速念三遍...）。虽然这份清单谈不上振奋人心，但势在必行。
  • 《最长的旅程》（The Longest Journey）： 鉴于其备受好评，这款冒险游戏绝对值得拥有一个独立的项目列表。
  • 《无人永生》（No One Lives Forever）： 为日益黑暗、睾酮过剩的 FPS 游戏类型注入了一股亟需的时髦、轻快与奇思妙想的新鲜空气（哪怕它完全搬套了《奥斯汀·鲍尔斯》的审美）。
  • 欧洲策略游戏（Aufbaustrategie）： 诸如《Settlers》（工人物语）系列特别是《Anno 1602》（创世纪 1602）在德国和欧洲超乎寻常的高人气，后者在世纪之交成为了德国有史以来最畅销的游戏。
  • 《Technomage: Return of Eternity》： 我在研究《Anno 1602》时，偶然发现了 Sunflower Interactive（《Anno 1602》背后的工作室）制作的这款冷门主机风动作冒险游戏。我发现自己莫名地被其吸引，尤其是被那从来不知道“讽刺”为何物的剧本所打动。
  • 数字文化： 在文化战线上，如果在时间上能安排得开，我正打算写一篇关于 Napster 及其引发的行业颠覆的文章。
  • Maxis & The Sims: We’re up to our eyebrows in this already, so I assume that no further explanation is required.
  • Driving Sims: A hugely neglected topic around these parts. I can’t remedy that entirely, but I can cover how these lifestyle-adjacent games came to be, alongside the one driving game I ever got seriously into (Hint: it involves Porsches).
  • The Lemmings Franchise: The somewhat anticlimactic later days of the series, which at least concluded with one last really good game.
  • Major RPGs: Deus Ex, Diablo II, Icewind Dale, and Baldur’s Gate II.
  • Russian CRPGs: The Russians are coming! Most notably with Evil Islands, an idiosyncratic but engaging take on the CRPG.
  • City-Builders: Impressions Games and their historical city-builders.
  • Her Interactive: I’ve been promising something about the folks who found fame and fortune—on a modest scale—through the unlikely vehicle of interactive Nancy Drew for years now. I’m finally going to do it this year. No, really, I am!
  • The Adventure Genre: The ongoing struggle for relevance: Discworld Noir; In Cold Blood; Stupid Invaders; Escape from Monkey Island; RealMyst; and Fairy Tale About Father Frost, Ivan, and Nastya (try saying that last one three times fast...). Not an overly heartening list, but needs must.
  • The Longest Journey: Given its critical acclaim, this adventure game definitely deserves its own standalone bullet point.
  • No One Lives Forever: A groovy, desperately needed breath of lightness and whimsy for the gamer-dark, testosterone-overloaded FPS genre (even if it does totally rip off the Austin Powers aesthetic).
  • European Strategy (Aufbaustrategie): The uncanny popularity in Germany and Europe of titles like the Settlers series and especially Anno 1602, the best-selling German game of all time at the turn of the millennium.
  • Technomage: Return of Eternity: I stumbled across this obscure curiosity of a console-style action-adventure from Sunflower Interactive (the studio behind Anno 1602) while researching the latter. I found myself weirdly charmed, not least by a script that has never heard of the concept of irony.
  • Digital Culture: On the cultural front, I’m toying with the idea of an article on Napster and the disruption it caused, if I can squeeze it in.

items.title: 对过往计划的反思与遗珠说明
items.text:
回顾我上一份清单，难得的是我这次相当好地兑现了我的承诺。一个例外是《Discworld Noir》，它被顺延到了上面提到的通用冒险游戏文章中。另一个是《The Longest Journey》，它直到 2000 年或更晚才走出挪威本土市场，因此放在这里正合适。

Looking back over my last list, I managed to do a reasonably good job of keeping my promises for a change. One exception is Discworld Noir, which gets pushed into the general adventure article above. Another is The Longest Journey, which didn’t reach markets beyond Norway until 2000 or later, so it fits fine here instead.

至于《Metal Gear Solid》（合金装备）……朋友们，我尽力了。我真的尽力了。但我觉得完全没办法以任何严肃的态度来看待它。如果我写它，我只会把所有时间都花在嘲笑它上面，这只会让你们当中喜欢这种日本主机美学的人更加讨厌我。对不起了，固蛇（Solid Snake）的粉丝们。这不是你们的问题，是我的问题。

As far as Metal Gear Solid goes… I tried, folks. I really did. But I found it impossible to take seriously in any sort of way. If I wrote about it, I’d just spend all my time making fun of it, and that would just make those of you who enjoy this Japanese console aesthetic hate me even more. I’m sorry, Solid Snake fans. It’s not you, it’s me.

像往常一样，非常欢迎大家为 2000 年提最后的建议，或者为未来的选题投稿。我不能保证对所有建议都予以采纳，但我会认真参考，前提是不超出日程排期、个人兴趣、专业知识以及我能把它们写得多么有趣。

As usual, last-minute suggestions for year 2000 and pitches for future topics are welcome. I can’t promise to act on all of them, but I will take them under advisement, bounded only by scheduling, personal interest, expertise, and how non-boring I can make them.

items.text: 许多软件工程师带着“校园幻想”进入大型科技公司，误以为只要默默做好本职工作就会自然获得优异绩效和回报。然而真实情况是，大型软件系统过于复杂，管理者无法独立评估每个人的实际贡献，职场高度依赖非正式网络与内部政治。想要成功，工程师必须主动为自己的工作争取功劳。但独占功劳往往适得其反，最成功的工程师反而懂得“大方将功劳分享出去”，以此建立同盟、扩大支持者阵营，并在发生故障时避免承受不成比例的甩锅。

items.title: 📌 概要
items.text:
许多软件工程师带着“校园幻想”进入大型科技公司——坚信只要默默做好工作就自然会获得优秀绩效和丰厚回报。但在现实中，大型软件系统极其复杂，管理者无法独立评估所有细节，职场很大程度上依赖于非正式网络和内部政治。要想取得成功，你必须主动为自己的工作争取功劳（Take credit）。然而，独吞功劳是适得其反的；最成功的工程师往往会大方地把功劳分享出去（Give away credit），以建立同盟、增加自己的支持者，并在出问题时保护自己免受不成比例的指责。

Many software engineers enter big tech with a "school fantasy"—the belief that doing good work quietly will naturally earn them top grades and rewards. In reality, large software systems are too complex for managers to independently assess, and workplaces rely heavily on informal networks and internal politics. Succeeding requires actively taking credit for your work. However, hoarding credit is counterproductive; the most successful engineers freely give credit away to build alliances, multiply their advocates, and protect themselves from disproportionate blame when things go wrong.

items.title: 1. “校园幻想”与真实职场
items.text:
工程师们经常抱怨说，让自己的工作成果变得可见应该是经理的职责，这样他们才能专注于纯粹的代码编写。

Engineers often complain that making their work visible should be their manager's job, allowing them to focus purely on writing code.

这种态度源于校园幻想：即期望职场运作得像大学一样，只要稳妥地完成布置的作业就能拿到好成绩。大型科技公司通过将办公室称为“园区（Campuses）”来积极鼓吹这种幻觉，以吸引聪明的毕业生。然而，这依然是工作，而不是学校。如果你把它当成学术环境来对待，你注定会感到挫败。

This attitude stems from the school fantasy: the expectation that the workplace operates like a university, where doing assigned work reliably earns you a good grade. Big tech companies actively encourage this illusion by calling their offices "campuses" to attract smart graduates. However, it is still work, not school. If you treat it like an academic environment, you are setting yourself up for frustration.

items.title: 2. 主动争取功劳
items.text:
许多新工程师面临的残忍一课是：你必须主动为自己的工作争取功劳。

A harsh lesson for many new engineers is that you must actively take credit for your work.

  • 隐形的施援者： 如果你在团队之外默默挽救了一个陷入困境的项目，功劳自然会流向项目负责人——更糟糕的是，你的经理可能会认为你的分心是一种缺乏专注的表现。

    • The Invisible Helper: If you quietly rescue a struggling project outside your team, the credit will naturally flow to the project lead—or worse, your manager may view your straying as a lack of focus.

  • 经理的盲区： 与学校里老师打分不同，你自己才是自己工作的领域专家。软件非常复杂，经理根本没有资格单凭自己评估你的技术表现。相反，他们依赖受信任的资深工程师来评估你的产出，在有毒的文化中，这可能会导致带有偏见的反馈、主观猜测甚至职场陷害。

    • The Manager’s Blind Spot: Unlike school, where a teacher grades assignments, you are the subject-matter expert on your own work. Software is so complex that managers are simply not qualified to assess your technical performance on their own. Instead, they rely on trusted senior engineers to gauge your output, which can lead to biased feedback, guesswork, or even workplace sabotage in toxic cultures.

  • 自我宣传的艺术： 经验丰富的工程师懂得如何主张功劳。他们会将取得的胜利告知经理，撰写详细介绍其解决方案的内部技术文章，并在管理链条中建立信任。参与其中只是应对企业现实的一部分。

    • The Art of Self-Promotion: Experienced engineers know how to claim credit. They inform their manager of wins, write technical internal posts detailing their solutions, and build trust across management chains. Engaging in this is simply part of navigating corporate reality.

items.title: 3. 大方分享功劳
items.text:
一个只知道独揽功劳的工程师——通常依赖一份只关注个人成就的“夸夸文档（Brag doc）”——忽略了一个关键的动态：往往通过将功劳分享出去，你反而能积累最多的功劳。

An engineer who only knows how to hoard credit—often relying on a "brag doc" focused solely on solo achievements—misses a crucial dynamic: you can often accumulate credit best by giving it away.

在大公司内部，升职和加薪很少由单一的直属经理说了算。相反，决定取决于一个由受信任工程师组成的隐藏网络，他们会非正式地评价你工作的价值。让这些人站在你这一边至关重要：

Inside large companies, promotions and raises are rarely decided by a single line manager. Instead, decisions rely on a hidden network of trusted engineers who informally judge the value of your work. Getting these people on your side is vital:

  • 共享聚光灯： 在公开场合感谢合作者，在你的项目文档中提及他们，并将其他人吸纳到你的个人项目中，将其转化为团队努力成果。

    • Share the Spotlight: Publicly thank collaborators, mention them in your project posts, and involve others in your individual projects to turn them into group efforts.

  • 共同投入： 一个共享的项目能为所有人带来光彩——你、你的同事以及你的经理。因为其他人也在项目的成功中占有股份，他们完全有理由去夸赞它并支持你。相反，嫉妒地死守项目会让你显得格格不入，并且让你在内部失去支持者。

    • Mutual Investment: A shared project reflects well on everyone—you, your peers, and your manager. Because others have a stake in the project's success, they have every reason to talk it up and support you. Conversely, jealously guarding a project makes you look antisocial and leaves you with no internal advocates.

items.title: 4. 镜像问题：归责
items.text:
追责（Blame）的运作规则与功劳完全相同。当发生复杂的技术故障时，经理会咨询他们的网络，以查明是谁搞砸了。因为软件系统是深度交织在一起的，有能力的工程师通常可以把责任归咎于他们想归咎的任何地方。

Blame operates by the exact same rules as credit. When a complex technical failure occurs, managers consult their networks to find out who screwed up. Because software systems are deeply interconnected, competent engineers can usually assign blame wherever they want.

  • 孤立的风险： 如果你是某个新项目中唯一独揽功劳的人，你就会成为避雷针。当出问题时，更广泛的工程师网络自然会有动力去指责那个他们没有参与过的、陌生且孤立的组件。

    • The Risk of Isolation: If you are the sole person taking credit for a new project, you become a lightning rod. When something goes wrong, the broader network of engineers will naturally be incentivized to fault the unfamiliar, isolated component they had no part in.

  • 协作的保护力量： 如果同一个工程师网络参与了你的项目并共享了功劳，他们维护该项目的可能性要高得多，而不太可能把所有责任单独推到你身上。

    • The Protective Power of Collaboration: If that same network was involved in your project and shared the credit, they are far more likely to defend it and less inclined to shift blame solely onto you.

items.title: 5. 总结
items.text:
功劳与归责是大厂真正的通用货币。因为经理依赖非公开的主观对话来评估技术角色，所以埋头苦干绝不足以保驾护航。

Credit and blame are the true currencies of big tech. Because managers rely on quiet, subjective conversations to evaluate technical roles, putting your head down and doing good work is never enough.

你必须通过 1:1 面谈、内部文章或其他渠道沟通你的影响力。然而，自我宣传也是有限度的。独占功劳之所以会失败，原因有二： 1. 分享功劳能让其他人为你的成功发声力挺。 2. 将功劳完全集中在自己身上会让你陷入孤立，并在出现复杂问题时容易承担全部责任。

You must communicate your impact through 1:1s, internal posts, or other channels. Yet, self-promotion has its limits. Hoarding credit fails for two reasons: 1. Sharing credit gets others to advocate for your success. 2. Concentrating credit entirely on yourself leaves you isolated and vulnerable to bearing the full weight of blame when complex problems arise.

items.title: 文章背景与核心概要
items.text: 本文回顾了美国电话网络从 20 世纪中叶贝尔系统（Ma Bell）高度集中的“一个系统、统一服务”租赁模式，向现代化终端设备零售市场演进的历史变迁。文章详细阐述了通过 Carterfone 裁决、FCC 的 Computer II 监管规程以及 1984 年 AT&T 的解体反垄断判决，电话终端如何被强制从网络中解耦。此外，文章揭示了这一转型所遗留的特殊历史现象：数以百万计的“嵌入式”租赁电话让许多消费者（尤其是老年人）在不知不觉中支付了数几十年的租赁费用，甚至催生出了延续至今的残存租赁产业。
path: 夹缝中的电话机：从贝尔系统垄断到残留租赁产业链

items.title: 执行概要
items.text:
在贝尔系统的鼎盛时期，美国电话网络作为一个庞大且高度集成的机器运作，其口号是“一个政策、一个系统、统一服务”。不同于现代化互联网将复杂性通过可互换设备和标准化接口推向边缘，20 世纪中叶的电话网络将复杂性集中在核心。电话机采用硬线连接、由专人高度维护，而且——关键在于——电话机是租赁而非购买的。

During the height of the Bell System, the American telephone network operated as a vast, tightly integrated machine under the motto "One Policy, One System, Universal Service." Unlike the modern Internet, which pushes complexity to the edges via interchangeable devices and standardized interfaces, the mid-century telephone network centralized its complexity. Telephones were hard-wired, heavily maintained, and—crucially—rented rather than owned.

1980 年代初期彻底打破了这一范式。通过里程碑式的反垄断诉讼、像 Computer II 这样的监管重组，以及 1984 年 AT&T 的最终解体，电话机被强制与电话网络解耦，并被推向了零售市场。

The early 1980s shattered this paradigm. Through landmark antitrust suits, regulatory overhauls like Computer II, and the eventual 1984 divestiture of AT&T, the telephone was forcefully decoupled from the telephone network and thrust into the retail market.

这一变革留下了一份奇特的企业遗产：数以百万计“嵌入”在合同中的租赁电话。虽然市场迅速接纳了消费者的自主选择，但许多消费者——尤其是老年人——在随后的数十年里继续按季度支付租赁费，从而引发了集体诉讼、企业拆分以及一个至今依然存活的奇特残余租赁产业。

This transformation left behind a strange corporate legacy: millions of "embedded" leased telephones. While the market quickly embraced consumer choices, many consumers—particularly the elderly—continued paying quarterly rental fees for decades, spawning class-action lawsuits, corporate spinoffs, and a bizarre residual leasing industry that survives to this day.

items.title: 1. “喂声机器”与租赁电话时代
items.text:
在其全盛时期，AT&T 的电话网络感觉不像是一系列独立设备的集合，而更像是一台单一的巨大机器。当订户签署服务合同后，“贝尔老妈妈”（Ma Bell）会负责安装电话、维护本地线路、处理维修，如果服务被取消，还会派人来把电话取走。

At its apex, AT&T's telephone network felt less like a collection of separate devices and more like a single, massive machine. When subscribers signed up for service, "Ma Bell" installed the phone, maintained the local loop, handled repairs, and—if service was canceled—came by to take the phone away.

在需要高维护成本的时代，租赁电话在实践中是非常合理的： * 技术需求： 早期电话需要本地电池或专门的接线配置。 * 兼容性与同线电话（Party Lines）： 复杂的选择性响铃同线电话和各异的交换机设备意味着，一台安装不当的电话可能会破坏整个社区的服务。 * 声誉管理： 为了保护网络的完整性并确保统一的质量，电话公司要求对客户前端设备（CPE）拥有完全的控制权。

Leasing phones made practical sense in an era requiring high maintenance: * Technical Demands: Early phones required local batteries or specialized wiring configurations. * Compatibility & Party Lines: Complex selective-ringing party lines and varying exchange equipment meant that a single incorrectly installed phone could disrupt service across an entire neighborhood. * Reputation Management: To protect the network's integrity and ensure uniform quality, the phone company demanded total control over Customer Premises Equipment (CPE).

然而，到了 20 世纪 60 和 70 年代，维护拥有 25 年历史的 Western Electric 电话舰队所带来的财务劣势，促使运营公司转向零售模式，从而孕育了 PhoneCenter 体验店和模块化电话插孔。

However, by the 1960s and 70s, the financial downsides of maintaining a fleet of 25-year Western Electric phones pushed operating companies toward a retail model, giving birth to PhoneCenters and modular telephone jacks.

items.title: 2. 反垄断压力与模块化竞争的诞生
items.text:
AT&T 对反垄断审查并不陌生。美国司法部 1949 年发起的一项诉讼旨在遏制 AT&T 如何利用其在电话服务上的自然垄断来控制相邻市场。随后的同意判决强制 AT&T 退出新兴的、不受监管的计算机行业（实际上为 IBM 扫清了道路），同时允许其继续作为受监管的公共承运人（Common Carrier）。

AT&T was no stranger to antitrust scrutiny. A 1949 Department of Justice suit sought to curb how AT&T leveraged its natural monopoly on phone service to control adjacent markets. The resulting consent decree forced AT&T out of the nascent, unregulated computer industry (effectively clearing the path for IBM) while allowing it to remain a regulated common carrier.

items.title: Carterfone 裁决与第三方零售
items.text:
数十年来，连接非贝尔设备需要从 AT&T 租赁昂贵的保护性连接装置（PCA）。在里程碑式的 Hush-A-Phone (1956) 和 Carterfone (1968) 裁决之后，FCC 废除了这些限制。到 1975 年，新规允许消费者购买并插接第三方电话机，前提是设备符合技术标准并在 FCC 备案登记。

For decades, connecting non-Bell equipment required expensive Protective Connecting Arrangements (PCAs) leased from AT&T. Following the landmark Hush-A-Phone (1956) and Carterfone (1968) rulings, the FCC dismantled these restrictions. By 1975, new rules allowed consumers to purchase and plug in third-party telephones, provided they met technical standards and registered with the FCC.

突然之间，消费者有了两种选择：支付绑定的月租费，或者直接购买一台电话。州监管机构很快强制电话公司在每月账单上单独列出租赁费用，给租赁模式带来了沉重打击。

Suddenly, consumers had two choices: pay a bundled monthly lease fee or buy a phone outright. State regulators soon forced telephone companies to separately itemize lease costs on monthly bills, dealing a major blow to the leasing model.

items.title: 3. Computer II 规程与企业迷宫
items.text:
随着计算机和电信开始通过分时复用和早期数据网络相互融合，FCC 启动了计算机调查（Computer Inquiry）程序，以防止受监管的垄断实体压垮新兴的数字竞争。

As computers and telecommunications began to blur through time-sharing and early data networks, the FCC launched the Computer Inquiry proceedings to prevent a regulated monopoly from crushing nascent digital competition.

  • Computer I (1966)： 试图通过严格的结构分离，将“通信服务”（受监管）与“数据处理”（不受监管）区分开来。
  • Computer II (1976)： 将定义转变为“基础服务”（底层传输网络）和“增强服务”（数据处理或存储）。
  • Computer I (1966): Attempted to separate "communications" (regulated) from "data processing" (unregulated) via strict structural separation.
  • Computer II (1976): Shifted definitions to "basic services" (the underlying transmission network) and "enhanced services" (data manipulation or storage).

在 Computer II 框架下，终端设备（电话机）被归类为增强服务。因此，AT&T 被迫成立了一个严格分离的子公司来处理消费级产品和计算机业务。这直接导致了 1982 年 American Bell 的诞生，随后改名为 AT&T Information Systems 和 AT&T Consumer Products。

Under Computer II, terminal equipment (telephones) was grouped with enhanced services. Consequently, AT&T was forced to form a strictly separated subsidiary to handle consumer products and computers. This gave rise to American Bell in 1982, later rebranded as AT&T Information Systems and AT&T Consumer Products.

items.title: 4. 1984 年大解体：贝尔系统的分裂
items.text:
与 FCC 的裁决平行推进的是，美国政府诉 AT&T 案在 1982 年达成了修改后的最终判决（MFJ）。1984 年 1 月 1 日，AT&T 剥离了其本地运营公司（即贝尔地区运营公司，BOCs）。

Running parallel to the FCC's rulings, United States v. AT&T culminated in the 1982 Modified Final Judgment (MFJ). On January 1, 1984, AT&T divested its local operating companies (the Bell Operating Companies, or BOCs).

解体给电话租赁领域带来了巨大震动： * 品牌禁令： AT&T 被禁止在非受监管实体上使用“Bell”商标，迫使 American Bell 再次更名为 AT&T Technologies。 * 独立账单： 租赁的电话机被转移至 AT&T Consumer Products，导致消费者收到关于本地服务和设备租赁的完全独立的账单。 * 困惑的 BOCs： 虽然本地运营公司最初被禁止租赁电话，但该限制在解体后被解除。然而，面对繁荣的零售市场和来自 AT&T 遗产租赁的竞争，大多数 BOCs 完全放弃了租赁业务。

Divestiture sent shockwaves through the telephone leasing landscape: * The Brand Ban: AT&T was prohibited from using the "Bell" trademark for non-regulated entities, forcing American Bell to rebrand yet again to AT&T Technologies. * Separate Bills: Leased telephones were transferred to AT&T Consumer Products, resulting in consumers receiving entirely separate bills for local service and equipment rentals. * The Baffled BOCs: While local operating companies were initially barred from leasing phones, that restriction lifted post-divestiture. However, facing a booming retail market and competition from AT&T's legacy leases, most BOCs abandoned leasing entirely.

items.title: 5. 租赁电话的漫长余晖
items.text:
尽管新租赁业务断崖式下跌，但数以百万计“嵌入”在旧合同中的遗产电话仍然处于使用状态。AT&T、Lucent Technologies（1996 年剥离）以及一系列晦涩的实体（包括 North Street Consumer Phone Services 和 QLT Consumer Lease Services）继承了这些残存的合同。

While new leases plummeted, millions of "embedded" legacy phones remained in service. AT&T, Lucent Technologies (spun off in 1996), and a succession of obscure entities—including North Street Consumer Phone Services and QLT Consumer Lease Services—inherited these remaining contracts.

items.title: 被遗忘的租赁陷阱
items.text:
到了 20 世纪 90 年代，租赁电话对大多数美国人来说已成为遥远的回忆。然而，数十万消费者（其中很大一部分是老年人）继续按季度支付设备费用——在数十年的时间里有时总计达数千美元——而这些电话机他们早在多年前就已更换或扔掉。

By the 1990s, leased telephones were a distant memory for most Americans. However, hundreds of thousands of consumers (disproportionately elderly) continued paying quarterly equipment fees—sometimes totaling thousands of dollars over decades—for phones they had long since replaced or thrown away.

  • 2002 年集体诉讼： 多个州的诉讼最终合并为一项针对欺诈性账单的全国性集体诉讼。诉讼设立了 3 亿美元的赔偿基金，但由于消费者意识淡薄和索赔缺乏，最终仅赔付了不到 1000 万美元。
  • 存续至今： 数十年后的今天，像 QLT 这样的公司 credit 依然维护着一小部分遗产租赁客户，继续为诞生于 20 世纪中叶“一个政策、一个系统、统一服务”时代的硬件收取每月或每季度的费用。
  • The 2002 Class Action: Lawsuits across multiple states were combined into a national class action alleging deceptive billing. A $300 million settlement fund was established, but due to poor consumer awareness and lack of claims, less than $10 million was ultimately paid out.
  • Surviving Today: Decades later, companies like QLT still maintain a small roster of legacy lease customers, continuing to collect monthly or quarterly fees for hardware introduced during the mid-century era of "One Policy, One System, Universal Service."

items.title: 脚注
items.text:
1. 选择性响铃： 与普遍误解相反，选择性响铃在同线电话上很常见，尤其是在城市地区。电信局向精密切割的螺线管发送不同的交流响铃频率，只允许特定目标电话响铃。
  1. Selective Ringing: Contrary to popular belief, selective ringing was common on party lines, especially in urban areas. Central offices sent different A/C ringing frequencies to carefully tuned solenoids, allowing only a single targeted phone to ring.
  1. 双音频按键附加费： 通过租赁模型升级到按键电话（Touch-Tone）的便利性受到很大削弱，因为电话公司通常仅为按键音频服务就额外收取每月费用。
  1. Touch-Tone Surcharges: The convenience of upgrading to a touch-tone phone via a leased model was heavily undercut by the fact that phone companies typically charged an extra monthly fee just for touch-tone service.
  1. 灰色地带： 事实证明，对于 FCC 来说，划清计算机网络与通信网络之间的界线极其困难，因为早期的消息传递系统经常需要协议转换。
  1. The Gray Area: Drawing a hard line between computer networks and communication networks proved exceptionally difficult for the FCC, as early messaging systems frequently required protocol conversions.
  1. Western Electric 的命运： 虽然 Western Electric 解体了，但其许多经典设计通过 Cortelco 等制造商得以延续，后者购买了追溯至 20 世纪 50 年代的生产许可。
  1. The Fate of Western Electric: While Western Electric dissolved, many of its classic designs live on through manufacturers like Cortelco, which purchased production licenses dating back to the 1950s.
  1. 企业壳公司游戏： AT&T 及其剥离公司内部的企业重组创造了持续数十年的多层责任——甚至将 National Cash Register (NCR) 等无关实体拖入了历史法律责任中。
  1. Corporate Shell Games: Corporate reorganizations within AT&T and its spinoffs created layers of liability that persisted for decades—even dragging unrelated entities like National Cash Register (NCR) into legacy legal liabilities.

items.title: 室内绿植真的能吸收你呼出的二氧化碳吗？
path: 室内绿植真的能吸收你呼出的二氧化碳吗？

items.title: 文章背景与核心概要
items.text: 在室内摆放绿色植物以改善空气质量、吸收人类呼出的二氧化碳（CO₂）是一个流传广泛的流行观念。然而，从物理学与生物化学的角度精确计算，要抵消一个成年人每天产生的约 1 公斤 CO₂，需要工厂级别的室内农场、数千瓦的高功率专业补光灯以及不断生长的巨幅植物墙。最终科学定量分析表明，摆放绿植对于降低室内二氧化碳浓度微乎其微，最简单高效的方法依然是开窗通风。
path: 室内绿植真的能吸收你呼出的二氧化碳吗？

items.title: 概要
items.text:
虽然在房间里摆满植物以抵消人类产生的二氧化碳是一个很受欢迎的想法，但物理学原理却给出了相反的答案。要中和普通成年人每天产生的约 1 公斤 CO₂，你需要一个工业级规模的室内农场、数千瓦的专业照明设备以及一面巨大且不断生长的植被墙。归根结底，降低室内 CO₂ 最有效的方式依然是那个谦逊、低科技的方案：打开窗户。

While it is a popular idea that filling a room with plants can offset human carbon dioxide production, the physics suggests otherwise. To neutralize the ~1 kg of CO₂ an average human produces daily, you would need an industrial-scale indoor farm, thousands of watts of specialized lighting, and a massive, ever-growing wall of vegetation. Ultimately, the most efficient way to manage indoor CO₂ remains the humble, low-tech solution: opening a window.
path: 室内绿植真的能吸收你呼出的二氧化碳吗？

items.title: 理论上的门槛
items.text:
人类每小时大约产生 1 摩尔的 CO₂。植物通过光合作用将 CO₂ 转化为氧气和葡萄糖。然而，驱动这一化学反应所需的能量是相当巨大的。即使假设拥有完美光合效率的“魔法”植物，仅仅处理这些碳，你也需要持续输入 132.5 瓦的功率。

Humans produce approximately one mole of CO₂ per hour. Plants, through photosynthesis, convert CO₂ into oxygen and glucose. However, the energy required to drive this chemical reaction is significant. Even with "magical" plants operating at perfect efficiency, you would need a continuous power input of 132.5 watts just to process that amount of carbon.
path: 室内绿植真的能吸收你呼出的二氧化碳吗？

items.title: 生物学的现实约束
items.text:
现实世界的物理约束使这一目标变得极其困难：

Real-world constraints make this goal significantly harder:

  • 光子利用率低： 植物无法吸收每一个光子。在反射、透射以及非光合作用组织的吸收过程中，会损失极大的能量。
  • 呼吸作用： 植物不仅仅储存碳，它们还会消耗很大一部分碳来维持自身生存，并将这些 CO₂ 重新释放回你的房间。
  • 热量与照明： 要达到必要的光合作用速率，你需要让房间浸泡在大约 918 瓦的纯红光中。如果使用标准 LED 植物生长灯，这需要近 2000 瓦的电功率——基本上相当于全功率运行几个电暖器。
  • Photon Efficiency: Plants don't capture every photon. Between reflection, transmission, and absorption by non-photosynthetic tissue, you lose a massive amount of energy.
  • Respiration: Plants don't just store carbon; they burn a large portion of it to stay alive, releasing that CO₂ right back into your room.
  • Heat and Light: To achieve the necessary photosynthetic rate, you would need to bathe your room in roughly 918 watts of pure red light. Using standard LED grow lights, this would require nearly 2,000 watts of power—essentially running several space heaters at full blast.
path: 室内绿植真的能吸收你呼出的二氧化碳吗？

items.title: 空间面积的限制
items.text:
植物存在“饱和点”——即它们一次能处理的光照上限。根据典型室内植物的光合作用能力计算，你需要至少 17.6 平方米的叶面积才能跟上你自身的呼吸消耗。这相当于一面超过 4 米宽、4 米高且密集种满蕨类植物的植物墙。

Plants have a "saturation point"—a limit to how much light they can process at once. Based on the photosynthetic capacity of a typical houseplant, you would need at least 17.6 square meters of leaf surface area to keep up with your own respiration. This is equivalent to a wall over 4 meters wide and 4 meters tall, packed solid with ferns.

items.title: 生物质积累难题
items.text:
如果植物成功地从空气中移除了碳，这些碳必须有去处。为了封存你呼出的碳，你的室内花园每天需要产生大约 4.6 公斤的新植物生物质。除非你准备好每月从家里修剪、采收并运出 140 公斤的植物材料，否则这些碳并没有被真正封存——它只是在你的客厅里循环。

If a plant successfully removes carbon from the air, that carbon must go somewhere. To sequester the carbon you exhale, your indoor garden would need to produce roughly 4.6 kg of new plant matter every single day. Unless you are prepared to prune, harvest, and remove 140 kg of plant matter from your home every month, the carbon isn't being sequestered—it’s simply cycling through your living room.

items.title: 结论与判决
items.text:
如果你想降低室内的 CO₂ 浓度，数学计算给出了清晰的解答：

If you want to reduce your indoor CO₂ levels, the math is clear:

  1. 建造一个工业级规模的室内农场。
  2. 称重整个系统。
  3. 等待两周。
  4. 再次称重。
  5. 用增加的质量除以你自己的体重，看看你到底抵消了多少 CO₂。
  6. 打开窗户。
  1. Build an industrial-scale indoor farm.
  2. Weigh the entire system.
  3. Wait two weeks.
  4. Weigh it again.
  5. Divide the weight gain by your own body mass to see how much CO₂ you’ve actually offset.
  6. Open a window.

path: 我如何在本博客中使用 AI

items.title: 文章背景与核心概要
items.text:
受 LessWrong 相关文章启发，作者详细阐述了在其个人技术博客中应用 AI 的核心原则与具体工作流。博客秉承“在公共场合学习”的理念，坚持所有文章文本与核心学习代码均由人工亲自编写，而将 AI 定位为辅助工具。AI 被广泛应用于创意构思、橡胶鸭调试、代码审查以及多模型编辑协同审查，但明确拒绝让 AI 代理全盘代劳，以保持低层探索的乐趣与学习摩擦感。

概要： 受一篇类似的 LessSword 文章 启发，本文阐述了本博客如何使用 AI。核心理念非常简单：AI 负责发现问题，我亲自动手解决。 虽然文本和核心学习代码严格由人工生成，以保持“公开学习”的精神，但 AI 在构思、代码审查、多阶段编辑反馈以及处理样板任务中发挥着强有力的支持作用。

Summary: Inspired by a similar LessSword post, this article outlines how AI is utilized on this blog. The core philosophy is simple: AIs identify problems, and I fix them myself. While text and core learning code are strictly human-generated to preserve the "learn in public" ethos, AI plays a heavy supporting role in ideation, code review, multi-stage editorial feedback, and handling boilerplate tasks.
path: 我如何在本博客中使用 AI

items.title: 创意构思与运行实验
items.text:
每篇文章都基于原创想法和动手实践。对于大型编程项目（比如从零构建和训练 GPT-2），我会保持与 ChatGPT 或 Claude 的长期对话。因为这些项目的真正价值在于个人的学习过程，所以我采取了深思熟虑的措施来防止 AI 替我思考：

Every post is based on original ideas and hands-on work. For large-scale coding projects (like building and training GPT-2 from scratch), I maintain ongoing chat sessions with ChatGPT or Claude. Because the true value of these projects lies in the personal learning process, I take deliberate steps to prevent AI from doing my thinking:

  • 橡胶鸭模式： 当 AI 开始解释本应由我自己去发现的概念时，我会跳过阅读，直接滚动到输入框，引导它扮演小黄鸭调试的角色。

    • Rubber Duck Mode: When an AI starts explaining concepts I should discover myself, I skip reading, scroll straight to the input field, and redirect it into a rubber duck debugging role.

  • 代码审查： 对于复杂且相互依赖的项目，我会将代码粘贴到对话中以检查 bug。我的严格指令是：指出缺陷，但不要编写修复代码。

    • Code Review: For complex, interdependent projects, I will paste code into a chat session to check for bugs. My strict instruction: point out the flaws, but do not write the fixes.

items.title: 编辑委员会
items.text:
一旦我根据详细的项目笔记写完草稿，它就会进入一个多阶段的 AI 编辑流水线，旨在捕捉逻辑漏洞、技术错误和表达清晰度问题，同时绝不重写我的文字。

Once I finish drafting a post based on my detailed project notes, it goes through a multi-stage AI editorial pipeline designed to catch logical gaps, technical errors, and clarity issues without ever rewriting my words.

  1. Claude（第一轮）： 我将草稿粘贴到与 Claude 的新对话中。它会检查技术错误、遗漏步骤、过度解释和语法错误。

    1. Claude (First Pass): I paste the draft into a fresh chat with Claude. It looks for technical errors, missing steps, over-explanations, and grammatical mistakes.

  2. ChatGPT（第二轮）： 接下来是 ChatGPT，它要挑剔得多。它会检查参考链接（常常能捕获我训练代码中的隐蔽 bug），并指出与严谨技术术语相冲突的比喻。

    1. ChatGPT (Second Pass): Next comes ChatGPT, which is far more pernickety. It checks supporting links (often catching subtle bugs in my training code) and flags metaphors that clash with rigorous technical terminology.

  3. 多模型阵容： 最后，我会将草稿发送给轮换的其他大语言模型阵营（目前包括 DeepSeek、Grok、GLM-5.2 和 Kimi K3），以捕获前两者遗漏的内容，并跟进最新模型的性能表现。

    1. The Multi-Model Cast: Finally, I run the draft through a rotating cast of other LLMs (currently DeepSeek, Grok, GLM-5.2, and Kimi K3) to catch anything the first two missed and to stay updated on model capabilities.

  4. 人工最终润色： 我会在私人测试网站上进行最后通读——最好是在晚餐和一杯葡萄酒之后——以润色文风、消除过于正式的语言，并将可读性提升至最高。

    1. Final Human Polish: I do a final read-through on a private staging site—ideally after dinner and a glass of wine—to smooth out the prose, remove overly formal language, and maximize readability.

整个过程耗时从短篇博客的 30 分钟到大型专题文章的数小时不等。

The entire process takes anywhere from 30 minutes for a short post to a couple of hours for a major write-up.

items.title: AI 编程策略
items.text:
我对编程的原则与对写作的原则如出一辙：如果通过编写代码能够有所收获，我就亲自手写。

My rule for coding mirrors my rule for writing: If I would learn something by writing the code, I write it by hand.

  • 亲力亲为： 核心概念和逻辑始终手动实现。

    • Hands-on: Core concepts and logic are always implemented manually.

  • 任务下放： 没有任何教育价值的样板任务——例如使用 matplotlib 绘制损失曲线，或构建炫酷的 JavaScript 参数可视化工具——都会交给 AI 处理（不过只要代码片段是由 AI 生成的，我总会明确披露）。

    • Delegated: Boilerplate tasks that offer no educational value—such as plotting loss curves with matplotlib or building a fancy JavaScript parameter visualizer—are handed off to AI (though I always explicitly disclose when a snippet is AI-generated).

  • 摩擦力控制： 为了避免被失控的范围所困扰，我总是通过标准聊天界面请求博客代码，而不是使用像 Claude Code 或 Codex 这样的 Agent 系统。

    • Friction Control: To avoid getting bogged down by runaway scope, I always request blog code through standard chat interfaces rather than using agentic systems like Claude Code or Codex.

items.title: 拥抱 Agent，但暂不用于本博客
items.text:
虽然在日常生活管理和目标导向型项目中我高度依赖 OpenClaw、Codex 和 Claude Code 等 Agent 工具，但它们目前还不属于本博客。

While I rely heavily on agentic tools like OpenClaw, Codex, and Claude Code for general life management and goal-oriented projects, they don't belong on this blog yet.

因为本博客的目的是记录动手实践、底层探索的学习过程（例如从零开始理解大语言模型的工作原理），过度自动化会违背这一初衷。一旦我拥有了扎实的基础并希望专注于更宏观的技术勾勒，未来情况可能会发生变化，但就目前而言：

Because the purpose of this blog is to document hands-on, low-level learning (e.g., understanding how LLMs work from the ground up), heavy automation would defeat the purpose. That may change in the future once I have a solid foundation and wish to focus on broader strokes, but for now:

本博客中的每一个字[^3]以及几乎每一行代码都是手写的——即使我需要一个 AI 委员会来让我保持在正轨上并维持基本的连贯性。

Every word[^3] and almost every line of code on this blog is written by hand—even if I need a committee of AIs to keep me on track and borderline coherent.
