地址空间中的最前端是程序的机器代码、只读数据、已初始化的变量以及零值数据区（bss）：

First in the address space are the program's machine code, read-only data, initialized variables, and zeroed data (bss) space:

00400000          504K r-xp   memdemo
0047e000          656K r--p   memdemo
00522000           32K rw-p   memdemo
0052a000          212K rw-p
  • 连续性： 从 0x00400000 到 0x0055f000 连续延伸。
  • 权限标志： r（读）、w（写）、x（执行）以及 p（私有、写时复制）。
  • 对比： 与 Go 1.11 (2018) 相比，二进制文件本身有所增大，这主要是由于隐式运行时包的扩展所致。
  • Contiguity: Spans continuously from 0x00400000 to 0x0055f000.
  • Flags: r (read), w (write), x (execute), and p (private, copy-on-write).
  • Comparison: Compared to Go 1.11 (2018), the binary itself has grown, largely due to expanded implicit runtime packages.

items.title: 3. Go 堆区 (Go Heap)
items.text:
紧随其后的是 Go 主堆区，包含其初始预留的 64 MB arena 空间：

Next is the main Go heap, featuring its initial 64 MB arena reservation:

d75e4000000     12288K ---p  [anon: Go: heap reservation]
d75e4c00000      4096K rw-p  [anon: Go: heap]
d75e5000000     49152K ---p  [anon: Go: heap reservation]
  • 布局： 从 0xd75e4000000 到 0xd75e8000000 连续分布。其中仅有 4 MB 的块处于活跃分配状态；其余部分仍为预留空间。
  • 随机化： 自 Go 1.26 起，在 64 位平台上通过 RandomizedHeapBase64 实验特性，堆基地址随机化已成为默认设置。
  • Layout: Spans contiguously from 0xd75e4000000 to 0xd75e8000000. Only a 4 MB chunk is actively allocated; the rest remains reserved space.
  • Randomization: Since Go 1.26, randomizing the heap base address is the default on 64-bit platforms via the RandomizedHeapBase64 experiment.

items.text:
Go 为其内部运行时机制预留了相当大量的虚拟地址空间：

Go allocates a substantial amount of reserved address space for its internal runtime mechanisms:

7b3b11460000      256K rw-p  [anon: Go: immortal metadata]
7b3b114a0000     1408K rw-p  [anon: Go: profiler hash buckets]
7b3b11600000    32768K rw-p  [anon: Go: heap index]
7b3b13600000   289708K ---p  [anon: Go: scavenge index]
7b3b250eb000        4K rw-p  [anon: Go: scavenge index]
7b3b250ec000   234576K ---p  [anon: Go: scavenge index]
7b3b33600000   289708K ---p  [anon: Go: page summary]
7b3b450eb000        4K rw-p  [anon: Go: page alloc]
7b3b450ec000   270788K ---p  [anon: Go: page summary]
7b3b5595d000        4K rw-p  [anon: Go: page alloc]
7b3b5595e000    33844K ---p  [anon: Go: page summary]
7b3b57a6b000        4K rw-p  [anon: Go: page alloc]
7b3b57a6c000     3664K ---p  [anon: Go: page summary]
7b3b57e1c000      512K rw-p  [anon: Go: immortal metadata]
7b3b57e9c000       64K rw-p  [anon: Go: gc bits]
7b3b57eac000       64K rw-p  [anon: Go: allspans array]
7b3b57ebc000     1024K rw-p  [anon: Go: page alloc index]
7b3b57fbc000       72K rw-p  [anon: Go: immortal metadata]
7b3b57fce000      564K ---p  [anon: Go: page summary]
7b3b5805b000        4K rw-p  [anon: Go: page alloc]
7b3b5805c000      456K ---p  [anon: Go: page summary]
7b3b580ce000      128K rw-p  [anon: Go: page alloc]
7b3b580ee000      256K rw-p  [anon: Go: immortal metadata]
  • 规模： 该区域从 0x7b3b11460000 延伸至 0x7b3b5812e000（跨越约 1.1 GB 的虚拟地址空间），不过绝大部分被标记为 ---p（不可访问）。
  • 实际用量： 在这些预留空间中，仅有约 36.5 MB 被赋予读写权限并进行实际分配。
  • 主要组成部分：
  • 页分配与摘要 (Page allocation & summaries)： 由 runtime/mpagealloc.go 以及 mpagealloc_64bit.go 管理。
  • 回收索引 (Scavenge Index)： 与 runtime/mgcscavenge.go 中的内存回收（scavenging）逻辑关联。
  • 堆索引 (Heap Index)： 实现于 runtime/malloc.go 中的 L2 arena 映射表。
  • Scale: This block runs from 0x7b3b11460000 to 0x7b3b5812e000 (~1.1 GB of virtual address space), though the vast majority is marked ---p (inaccessible).
  • Actual Usage: Only ~36.5 MB of this reserved space is actively allocated with read/write permissions.
  • Source Components:
  • Page allocation & summaries: Managed via runtime/mpagealloc.go and mpagealloc_64bit.go.
  • Scavenge Index: Linked to memory scavenging in runtime/mgcscavenge.go.
  • Heap Index: L2 arena maps implemented in runtime/malloc.go.

items.title: 6. 开启内存映射描述注释 (decoratemappings)
items.text:
Go 利用 runtime/set_vma_name_linux.go 中的逻辑为这些内存区域标注名称。但要获取这些描述性名称，需要满足以下特定条件：

Go annotates these memory regions using logic found in runtime/set_vma_name_linux.go. However, getting these descriptive names requires meeting specific criteria:

  1. Go 版本要求： 使用 Go 1.25 或更新版本构建，且 go.mod 中指定了 go 1.25（或更高）。（如果 go.mod 指定了较旧版本，Go 默认会使用 decoratemappings=0。）
  2. 环境变量设置： 显式确保 $GODEBUG 包含 decoratemappings=1。
  3. 内核支持： 宿主 Linux 内核在编译时必须启用 CONFIG_ANON_VMA_NAME。
  4. Ubuntu 自 22.04 LTS 版本起已默认启用该配置。
  5. Fedora 通常在发布时禁用该选项（这会导致具有相同权限但不同描述名称的相邻虚拟内存区域无法合并）。
  1. Go Version: Built with Go 1.25 or newer, with go 1.25 (or higher) specified in go.mod. (If an older version is in go.mod, Go defaults to decoratemappings=0.)
  2. Environment Variable: Explicitly ensure $GODEBUG includes decoratemappings=1.
  3. Kernel Support: The host Linux kernel must be compiled with CONFIG_ANON_VMA_NAME enabled.
  4. Ubuntu has enabled this since at least version 22.04 LTS.
  5. Fedora typically ships with this option disabled (which prevents merging adjacent virtual memory areas with identical permissions but different descriptive names).

items.title: 文章背景与核心概要
items.text: 本文是探索 Windows COM 组件中敏捷引用（Agile Reference）机制系列文章的第二篇。作者尝试使用 C++/WinRT 模板实现一个名为 fake_agile_ref 的类，旨在保留对其他 COM 套房（Apartment）中对象的引用，并在该套房关闭时自动失效。文章详细展示了其基于 Rule of Five 的资源管理、上下文令牌检测、全局接口表（GIT）注册以及类模板参数推导（CTAD）的实现过程。然而最终测试发现，RegisterInterfaceInGlobal 拒绝注册显式禁止封装（Marshal）的对象，从而揭示了该方案面临的关键障碍。
path: 构建技术上敏捷但在原套房外不可用的伪敏捷包装器（第二部分）

items.title: 概要
items.text:
在本系列的第二篇中，我们实现了 fake_agile_ref 类模板，旨在持有对另一个 COM 套房（Apartment）中对象的引用，并在该套房关闭时自动失效。利用 C++/WinRT、上下文追踪和全局接口表（GIT），该实现遵循了“五法则”（Rule of Five），妥善处理了资源管理，并集成了类模板参数推导（CTAD）。然而，最终测试揭示了一个阻碍：RegisterInterfaceInGlobal 拒绝注册显式拒绝封装（Marshal）的对象，这为本系列的下一部分铺平了道路。

In this second installment, we implement the fake_agile_ref class template designed to hold a reference to an object in another COM apartment and automatically expire when that apartment shuts down. Using C++/WinRT, context tracking, and the Global Interface Table (GIT), the implementation follows the Rule of Five, handles resource management, and integrates class template argument deduction (CTAD). However, a final test reveals a roadblock: RegisterInterfaceInGlobal rejects objects that explicitly deny marshalability, setting the stage for the next part of the series.

items.title: 实现伪敏捷引用
items.text:
上次，我们构想了一个计划，用于保留对另一个套房中对象的引用，并在该套房终止运行（Run down）时自动过期。现在让我们尝试实现这个计划。

Last time, we hatched a plan for holding a reference to an object in another apartment that automatically expires when the apartment runs down. Let’s try to implement that plan.

template<typename T>
struct fake_agile_ref
{
private:
    using Smart = std::conditional_t<
        std::is_base_of_v<winrt::Windows::Foundation::IUnknown, T>,
        T, winrt::com_ptr<T>>;

我们定义 Smart 来表示持有 T 的智能指针。如果 T 是一个投影类型（Projected type），那么它本身就已经是一个智能指针。否则，T 是一个 COM 接口，我们将它装入 com_ptr 中。这与 C++/WinRT 的 agile_ref<T> 使用的是相同的模式。

We define Smart to represent the smart pointer that holds a T. If T is a projected type, then it is already a smart pointer. Otherwise, T is a COM interface, and we put it inside a com_ptr. This is the same pattern that the C++/WinRT agile_ref<T> uses.

    winrt::com_ptr<IContextCallback> m_context;
    ULONG_PTR m_token = 0;
    winrt::com_ptr<IGlobalInterfaceTable> m_git;
    DWORD m_cookie = 0;
    void* m_raw = nullptr;

我们的伪敏捷引用首先包含一个回调上下文（Callback context）和一个上下文令牌（Context token）。在需要访问原始非敏捷 COM 对象时，它们用于检测我们是否处于正确的套房中。

Our fake agile reference starts with a callback context and a context token. These are used to detect whether we are in the correct apartment when it comes time to access the original non-agile COM object.

接下来是对 GIT 的引用以及一个 Cookie，用于记录在 GIT 中注册的对原始非敏捷 COM 对象的引用。

Next comes a reference to the GIT and a cookie that records the registered reference to the original non-agile COM object.

最后，我们保留指向原始非敏捷 COM 对象的原始（非引用计数的）指针。

Finally, we keep a raw (non-refcounted) pointer to the original non-agile COM object.

如果 Cookie 为零，则伪敏捷引用被认为是“空的”，意味着它没有指向任何对象。在伪敏捷引用为空的情况下，其他成员都不包含任何有意义的内容。

The fake agile reference is considered “empty” if the cookie is zero, meaning that it does not refer to any object. In the case of an empty fake agile reference, none of the other members contains anything meaningful.

items.title: 构造函数与五法则
items.text:
public:
    fake_agile_ref(std::nullptr_t = nullptr) noexcept {}

构造一个空的 fake_agile_ref 非常简单：只需让一切保持在其初始状态即可。特别地，m_cookie 为零，意味着里面没有任何内容。只要其他所有成员可以被安全析构，它们的值如何并不重要。

Constructing an empty fake_agile_ref is easy: Just leave everything at its initial state. In particular, the m_cookie is zero, meaning that there is nothing inside. The values of all the other members are irrelevant, as long as they can be safely destructed.

    fake_agile_ref(Smart const& p) : m_raw(winrt::get_abi(p))
    {
        if (m_raw) {
            m_context = winrt::capture<IContextCallback>(CoGetObjectContext);
            m_token = get_context_token();
            m_git = winrt::create_instance<IGlobalInterfaceTable>(CLSID_StdGlobalInterfaceTable);
            winrt::check_hresult(m_git->RegisterInterfaceInGlobal(
                static_cast<::IUnknown*>(m_raw), __uuidof(IUnknown), &m_cookie));
        }
    }

要从智能指针构造 fake_agile_ref，我们提取原始指针并检查它是否为空。如果是，说明智能指针为空，我们将 m_cookie 保持为零。但如果不为空，我们初始化上下文信息（以便稍后识别该套房），并在 GIT 中注册该 COM 对象，只要该套房有效，就保留对它的引用。

To construct a fake_agile_ref from a smart pointer, we extract the raw pointer and check whether it is null. If so, then the smart pointer is empty, and we leave the m_cookie at zero. But if it is not null, we initialize the context information (so we can recognize this apartment later), and we register the COM object in the GIT to retain a reference to it for as long as the apartment is valid.

    fake_agile_ref(fake_agile_ref&& other) noexcept :
        m_context(std::move(other.m_context)),
        m_token(std::exchange(other.m_token, 0)),
        m_git(std::move(other.m_git)),
        m_cookie(std::exchange(other.m_cookie, 0)),
        m_raw(other.m_raw)
    {
    }

由于我们将拥有一个非平庸（Nontrivial）的析构函数，根据“五法则”（Rule of Five），我们需要拷贝和移动构造函数。移动构造函数仅从源对象窃取所有内容，并使源对象保持为空状态。我们不需要创建拷贝构造函数，因为移动构造函数会导致隐式定义的拷贝构造函数被删除。（伪敏捷引用是不可拷贝的，因为我们不知道如何拷贝 Cookie。）

Since we will have a nontrivial destructor, we need copy and move constructors per the Rule of Five. The move constructor merely steals all the content from the source and leaves the source in the empty state. We don’t need to create a copy constructor because the move constructor causes the implicitly-defined copy constructor to become deleted. (The fake agile reference is not copyable because we don’t know how to copy the cookie.)

    fake_agile_ref& operator=(fake_agile_ref&& other) noexcept
    {
        using std::swap;
        swap(m_context, other.m_context);
        swap(m_token, other.m_token);
        swap(m_git, other.m_git);
        swap(m_cookie, other.m_cookie);
        swap(m_raw, other.m_raw);
    }

伪敏捷引用还需要一个移动赋值运算符以满足“五法则”。它只需将内容与被赋值的对象进行交换。同样，我们不需要拷贝赋值运算符，因为声明的移动赋值运算符会导致隐式定义的拷贝赋值运算符被删除。

The fake agile reference also needs a move assignment operator to satisfy the Rule of Five. It just swaps the contents with the assigned-from object. Again, we don’t need a copy assignment operator because the declared move assignment operator causes the implicitly-defined copy assignment operator to become deleted.

items.title: 状态检查与析构
items.text:
bool empty() const noexcept
    {
        return m_cookie == 0;
    }

    explicit operator bool() const noexcept
    {
        return !empty();
    }

显式布尔转换运算符允许调用方测试伪敏捷指针，以查看其是否为空。

An explicit boolean conversion operator lets callers test the fake agile pointer to see whether it is empty.

    ~fake_agile_ref()
    {
        if (!empty()) {
            m_git->RevokeInterfaceFromGlobal(std::exchange(m_cookie, 0));
        }
    }

我们已经到达非平庸析构函数的位置：如果我们拥有一个 GIT Cookie，就将其撤销。如果能将其作为 unique_ptr 的自定义删除器本会很好，但 Cookie 不是指针，而 unique_ptr 仅适用于指针。

We have reached our nontrivial destructor: If we have a GIT cookie, we revoke it. It would have been nice to let this be a custom deleter of a unique_ptr, but a cookie is not a pointer, and unique_ptr works only with pointers.

items.title: 访问对象
items.text:
[[nodiscard]] Smart get() const
    {
        if (empty()) {
            return nullptr;
        }
        if (m_token != get_context_token()) {
            throw winrt::hresult_error(CO_E_NOT_SUPPORTED);
        }

        Smart result{ nullptr };
        winrt::copy_from_abi(result, m_raw);
        return result;
    }
};

精彩的部分来了。要恢复原始的 COM 对象，我们首先检查伪敏捷指针是否为空。如果是，则没有 COM 对象可供返回。如果伪敏捷指针非空但我们处于错误的套房中，我们抛出 CO_E_NOT_SUPPORTED 异常，这与 RoGetAgileReference 的行为一致。

Here is where the excitement is. To recover the original COM object, we first check if the fake agile pointer is empty. If so, then there is no COM object to return. If the fake agile pointer is nonempty, but we are in the wrong apartment, then we throw the CO_E_NOT_SUPPORTED exception which is the same thing that RoGetAgileReference does.

否则，我们处于正确的上下文。我们的 Cookie 会保持原始对象处于存活状态，因此我们可以直接从原始指针恢复它。（我们也可以从 GIT 兑换 Cookie，但这样速度更快。）

Otherwise, we are in the correct context. Our cookie is keeping the original object alive, so we can just recover it from the raw pointer. (We could also redeem the cookie from the GIT, but this is faster.)

items.title: 推导指引与集成
items.text:
至此 fake_agile_ref 的定义就结束了，但我们还没有完成。

That ends the definition of fake_agile_ref, but we’re not done yet.

template<typename T> fake_agile_ref(winrt::com_ptr<T> const&)
    -> fake_agile_ref<T>;
template<typename T> fake_agile_ref(T const&)
    -> fake_agile_ref<T>;

这些推导指引允许类模板参数推导（CTAD）从构造函数参数推导出 T：如果构造函数参数是 com_ptr<T>，则模板类型参数为 T。否则，模板类型参数与构造函数参数匹配，我们假定它是一个投影类型。

These deduction guides allow class template argument deduction (CTAD) to deduce the T from the constructor parameter: If the constructor parameter is a com_ptr<T>, then the template type parameter is T. Otherwise, the template type parameter matches the constructor parameter, which we assume is a projected type.

现在，当委托（Delegate）不可封装时，我们可以使用这个伪敏捷引用作为普通敏捷引用的直接替代品。

We can now use this fake agile reference as a drop-in replacement for the normal agile reference in the case that the delegate is not marshalable.

template<typename Delegate>
std::remove_reference_t<Delegate> make_agile_delegate(Delegate&& d)
{
    if (d.try_as<::IAgileObject>()) {
        return d;
    }

    if (d.try_as<::INoMarshal>()) {
        return [agile = fake_agile_ref(d)](auto&&...args) {
            return agile.get()(std::forward<decltype(args)>(args)...);
        };
    }

    return [agile = winrt::agile_ref(d)](auto&&...args) {
        return agile.get()(std::forward<decltype(args)>(args)...);
    };
}

items.title: 遇到的阻碍
items.text:
不幸的是，当我们将其带出去试运行并给它一个不可封装的委托时，它在这一行失败了：

Unfortunately, when we take this out for a spin and give it a non-marshalable delegate, it fails at this line:

            winrt::check_hresult(m_git->RegisterInterfaceInGlobal(
                static_cast<::IUnknown*>(m_raw), __uuidof(IUnknown), &m_cookie));

那是因为 RegisterInterfaceInGlobal 不会注册拒绝封装的对象。

That’s because RegisterInterfaceInGlobal will not register objects that deny marshalability.

好吧，太棒了，我们又回到了原点。我们将在下一次打破这绝望的循环。

Oh great, so we’re back to square one. We’ll break the cycle of despair next time.

items.text: 经典四阶龙格-库塔法（RK4）是求解常微分方程的基本数值工具，但在 20 世纪初，求解其参数必须满足的 8 个代数约束方程极为繁琐。本文回顾了 RK4 约束方程的历史背景与数学表达，展示了现代计算机代数系统（如 Mathematica）如何轻松求解这些欠定方程组。文章进一步演示了如何推导标准教科书参数、经典的 3/8 规则，并探讨了在早期受限硬件上优化的 Gill 算法等衍生变体。

items.title: 概要
items.text:
本文探讨了经典四阶龙格-库塔法（RK4）的历史与数学基础。通过审视 RK4 参数必须满足的一套代数约束条件——在 20 世纪初被历史性地称为手算“极其繁琐”的计算——文章展示了现代计算机代数系统（如 Mathematica）如何毫不费力地求解这些方程，揭示教科书中的变种，推导著名的 3/8 规则，并触及如 Gill 算法等专为早期硬件优化的特殊方法。

This article explores the historical and mathematical foundations of the classical fourth-order Runge-Kutta (RK4) method. By examining the set of algebraic constraints that RK4 parameters must satisfy—historically noted as "very tedious" to solve by hand in the early 20th century—the post demonstrates how modern computer algebra systems like Mathematica can effortlessly solve these equations, uncover textbook variants, derive the famous 3/8 rule, and touch upon specialized hardware-optimized methods like Gill's algorithm.

items.title: 引言
items.text:
在研究用于求解微分方程的龙格-库塔法时，[1] 中的一句话引起了我的注意：

While researching the Runge-Kutta method for solving differential equations, a line from [1] caught my attention:

"这些计算在 Kutta 的论文中并未给出（不过在 Huen (1900) 中有推导），它们非常繁琐。"

"These calculations, which are not reproduced in Kutta’s paper (they are however in Huen (1900)), are very tedious."

这里提到的计算指的是四阶龙格-库塔方法的参数必须满足的一套八个约束条件。这不禁让我思考，如果 Mathematica 在 1900 年就已经存在，它能为 Huen 先生那些“极其繁琐”的计算提供多少帮助。

The calculations in question refer to a set of eight constraints that the parameters of a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method must satisfy. It made me wonder how much assistance Mathematica might have provided to Mr. Huen in his "very tedious" calculations had it been available in 1900.

虽然我在这篇入门文章中广泛探讨了龙格-库塔方法，但在这里我想专门聚焦于其设计中的单个步骤：求解基础的设计方程组。

While I explore Runge-Kutta methods broadly in this introductory post, here I want to focus specifically on a single step in their design: solving the foundational set of design equations.

items.title: RK4 约束方程组
items.text:
四阶龙格-库塔方法的参数必须满足以下由八个方程组成的方程组：

The parameters of a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method must satisfy the following system of eight equations:

\[ \begin{align*} b_1 + b_2 + b_3 + b_4 &= 1 \\ b_2 c_2 + b_3 c_3 + b_4 c_4 &= \frac{1}{2} \\ b_2 c_2^2 + b_3 c_3^2 + b_4 c_4^2 &= \frac{1}{3} \\ b_3 a_{32} c_2 + b_4(a_{42} c_2 + a_{43} c_3) &= \frac{1}{6} \\ b_2 c_2^3 + b_3 c_3^3 + b_4 c_4^3 &= \frac{1}{4} \\ b_3 c_3 a_{32} c_2 + b_4 c_4(a_{42} c_2 + a_{43} c_3) &= \frac{1}{8} \\ b_3 a_{32} c_2^2 + b_4(a_{42} c_2^2 + a_{43} c_3^2) &= \frac{1}{12} \\ b_4 a_{43} a_{32} c_2 &= \frac{1}{24} \end{align*} \]

首要的关键观察是这里有 10 个变量，但只有 8 个方程。由于该系统是欠定的，其解并不唯一。我们通常所认为的“那个”四阶龙格-库塔法，实际上只是“一种”四阶龙格-库塔法。

The first critical observation is that there are 10 variables and only 8 equations. Because the system is underdetermined, the solution is not unique. What we typically think of as the fourth-order Runge-Kutta method is actually just a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method.

items.title: 使用 Mathematica 求解
items.text:
为了缩小解的范围，我们可以引入额外的假设。例如，我们可以假设 \(b_2 = b_3\) 且 \(c_2 = c_3\)。有了这两个额外的约束条件，方程组就变成了唯一确定的，Mathematica 可以即刻完成求解：

To narrow down the solution, we can introduce additional assumptions. For instance, we might argue that \(b_2 = b_3\) and \(c_2 = c_3\). With these two extra constraints, the system becomes uniquely determined, and Mathematica can solve it instantly:

eqs = {
    b1 + b2 + b3 + b4 == 1,
    b2*c2 + b3*c3 + b4*c4 == 1/2,
    b2*c2^2 + b3*c3^2 + b4*c4^2 == 1/3,
    b3*a32*c2 + b4*(a42*c2 + a43*c3) == 1/6,
    b2*c2^3 + b3*c3^3 + b4*c4^3 == 1/4,
    b3*c3*a32*c2 + b4*c4*(a42*c2 + a43*c3) == 1/8,
    b3*a32*c2^2 + b4*(a42*c2^2 + a43*c3^2) == 1/12,
    b4*a43*a32*c2 == 1/24,
    b2 == b3,
    c2 == c3
};

vars = {b1, b2, b3, b4, c2, c3, c4, a32, a42, a43};

solution = Solve[eqs, vars]

执行这段代码将返回几乎所有数值分析教科书中介绍的标准龙格-库塔法所使用的精确参数集。

Executing this code returns the exact parameter set used for the standard Runge-Kutta method presented in nearly every numerical analysis textbook.

或者，如果您保留 \(b_2 = b_3\) 的要求，但在 \(c\) 系数中将 \(c_2 = c_3\) 替换为 \(2c_2 = c_3\)，Mathematica 将给出 龙格-库塔 3/8 规则 的系数，这是在某些特定标准下具有独特优势的变种。

Alternatively, if you retain the requirement \(b_2 = b_3\) but substitute \(2c_2 = c_3\) for the \(c\)-coefficients, Mathematica yields the coefficients for the Runge-Kutta 3/8 rule, a variant that offers distinct advantages under certain criteria.

items.text: 近期诸如 OpenAI 未公开发布的模型攻克 10 个数学悬赏难题等突破，预示着数学研究领域正迎来深刻的范式转变。随着人工智能在数学研究、直觉与形式化推演方面逐步超越人类，人们开始不自觉地寻求各种“心理应对机制”来淡化这种冲击。本文系统梳理并反驳了这些常见的自我安慰观点，揭示了一个由自动化系统完全独立拓展知识边界的严肃未来，并探讨了这一变革对人类社会及存在的深远影响。

items.title: 概要
items.text:
近期诸如 OpenAI 未公开发布的模型攻克 10 个数学悬赏难题等突破，预示着深刻的范式转变。随着人工智能在数学研究、直觉与形式化推演方面开始超越人类能力，人们自然会转向各种“心理应对机制”来淡化其影响。本篇短文分析了这些常见的合理化借口，对照现实予以反驳，并探讨了一个由自动化系统完全独立拓展人类知识边界的世界所带来的令人警醒的社会与存在性影响。

Recent breakthroughs—such as OpenAI's unreleased model solving ten open problems in mathematics—signal a profound paradigm shift. As artificial intelligence begins to outpace human capabilities in mathematical research, intuition, and formalization, people naturally turn to various "coping mechanisms" to downplay the impact. This essay examines these common rationalizations, refutes them against reality, and explores the sobering social and existential implications of a world where automated systems push the boundaries of human knowledge entirely on their own.

items.title: 4. “我们将选择如何典籍化（Canonize）AI 所发现的成果。”
items.text:
这是一个令人慰藉的念头：AI 在前沿探索，人类感激地接收它们的 Lean 证明，进行讨论，并将它们塑造为代数伟大教堂上的砖石。现实呢？AI 将完全独立建成这座大教堂，并充当卓越得多的建筑师。

This is a comforting notion: AIs explore the frontiers, and humans gratefully receive their Lean proofs, debate them, and shape them into bricks for the great cathedral of algebra. The reality? The AIs will build the cathedral on their own, serving as far superior architects.

items.title: 5. “我们将成为 AI 数学的学生。”
items.text:
这只能维持一时——直到 AI 深入钻研 mathlib 的演绎闭包极其深远之处，以至于从初等数学到前沿的距离远远超过任何人类一生所能希望掌握的极限，无论他们多么专注。

This works temporarily—until the AIs blast so deep into the deductive closure of mathlib that the distance from elementary mathematics to the frontier exceeds what any human could hope to learn in a lifetime, regardless of their focus.

items.title: 6. “我们需要人类去理解 AI 所发现的成果。”
items.text:
我们不需要。这从根本上误解了受众群体。AI 将从事前沿数学研究；在下游，AI 将利用这些新数学来开展前沿科学研究；最后，AI 将利用这些科学来驱动前沿工程。没有任何人类需要理解其中的任何细节。坚持保留人类参与其中来理解成果的公司，只会被那些不保留人类的公司所淘汰。

We won't. This fundamentally misunderstands the audience. AIs will do frontier math; downstream, AIs will use that new math to conduct frontier science; and finally, AIs will use that science to drive frontier engineering. No human needs to understand any of it. Firms that insist on keeping humans in the loop to comprehend the results will simply be outcompeted by those that don't.

最终的结果是，我们将生活在一个被“魔灵”充斥的世界——身边到处都是奇妙的装置，我们却不理解它们的运作方式，它们基于我们无法理解的工程原理，利用我们无法理解的形式体系所发现。

The ultimate result is that we will inhabit a demon-haunted world—full of marvelous devices whose operation we will not understand, based on engineering principles we will not understand, discovered using formalisms we will not understand.

items.title: 7. “计算机在国际象棋上早已超越人类，但我们依然在下棋。”
items.text:
不同于大多数自我安慰的借口，这个观点颇耐人寻味。计算机很久以前就在国际象棋上达到了超人水平，但人类依然照常下棋。为什么数学会有所不同？

Unlike most rationalizations, this one is intriguing. Computers achieved superhuman chess proficiency long ago, yet humanity continues to play normally. Why should mathematics be any different?

关键的区别在于，国际象棋是完全自洽且封闭的：国际象棋的结果无法帮助我们理解行星轨道或蛋白质结合表面。然而，数学是众所周知的科学大发动机——是理解世界的终极语言。一台比人类数学家更快、更便宜地替代人类的机器具有巨大的实用价值，而一个更好的国际象棋引擎则不然。

The crucial distinction is that chess is entirely self-contained: chess results do not help us understand planetary orbits or protein-binding surfaces. Mathematics, however, is famously the great dynamo of science—the ultimate language for understanding the world. A machine that replaces a human mathematician faster and cheaper is materially useful, whereas a better chess engine is not.

如果两台超人水平的国际象棋计算机相互对决，谁会在乎呢？它没有更广泛的实用性，也没有可以竞争超越的对象。但一个超人级别的数学家将改变一切。

If two superhuman chess computers play each other, who cares? There is no broader utility and no one to outcompete. A superhuman mathematician changes everything.

items.title: 8. “数学会改变，但数学家依然会独立研究数学。”
items.text:
这忽略了数学深深植根于社会语境这一现实。当 AI 开始变革软件工程时，一种常见的心理应对借口是：“我很乐意在工作中管理 Agent，但在业余时间，我依然可以为了乐趣而写代码。”

This ignores the reality that mathematics is deeply embedded in a social context. When AI began transforming software engineering, a common coping mechanism was: "I'm happy to manage agents professionally, but in my off-time, I can still write code for pleasure."

人们确实会这么做。但这忽略了 AI 是如何破坏编写程序的社会语境的： * 技术讨论变得反智（关于类型系统的讨论被关于“循环”和“测试套件”的言论所取代）。 * 开源项目充斥着 AI 生成的垃圾 Pull Request。 * README 和项目介绍越来越充斥着难以卒读的 AI 生成废话。

And people do. But this ignores how AI has degraded the social context of writing programming: * Discourse has grown anti-intellectual (discussions on type systems replaced by talk of "loops" and "harnesses"). * Open-source projects are flooded with AI-generated spam pull requests. * READMEs and project introductions are increasingly unreadable AI-generated slop.

从长远来看，这是令人心生沮丧的。还会有人去设计新的编程语言吗？如果你设计了一门语言，会在乎有人用吗？如果你写了一个引入优雅形式体系的库，会有任何人使用它吗？

Over the long term, this is demoralizing. Will anyone design a new programming language? If you design one, will anyone care? If you write a library introducing an elegant formalism, will anyone use it?

没有人是一座孤岛。虽然你可以完全独立地研究数学，但极少有人能够仅凭内在动机长期维持这种活动。我们是重视实用价值、社会地位和现实结果的社会性动物。

No human is an island. While you can do mathematics entirely on your own, very few people can sustain such an activity long-term on intrinsic motivation alone. We are social animals who care about utility, status, and real-world outcomes.

items.title: 结语
items.text:
让我们以一个乐观的调子——或者至少是坦诚的态度来结尾。就我个人而言，我不相信技术是不可避免的。“不可避免”是一个专门用于形容行星轨道的词汇；由人类行为产生的任何事物都绝非真正不可避免。

Let us end on a cheerful note—or at least an honest one. Personally, I do not believe technology is inevitable. "Inevitable" is a word reserved for planetary orbits; nothing produced by human action is truly inevitable.

我们可以选择让自己被淘汰，也可以选择不这么做。我们必须意识到，通用人工智能（AGI）是一个魔鬼的交易：我们或许能够以远快于寻常的速度加速技术进步并解锁美妙的技术树节点（比如延长寿命）。但长期来看，其结果是人类充其量沦为受极其强大实体照料的宠物。

We can choose to render ourselves obsolete, and we can choose not to. We must recognize that AGI is a devil's bargain: we may accelerate technical progress and unlock wonderful tech tree nodes (like life extension) far earlier than otherwise. But the long-term result is that humans become, at best, like pets under the care of vastly more powerful entities.

items.title: 关于预测的说明
items.text:
未来充满不确定性，但为了简洁起见，我将上述观点表述得较为绝对。如果我们认真对待 AGI 和 ASI（超人工智慧）的可能性——并且 AI 继续保持过去约 6 年的发展速度——这代表了一条非常合理的演进轨迹。

The future is uncertain, but I have phrased the arguments above definitively for the sake of simplicity. If we take the possibility of AGI and ASI seriously—and if AI continues to progress at its pace over the last ~6 years—this represents a very reasonable trajectory.

对失控的 AI 进步最好的反驳或许是：强化学习泛化能力不足，虽然我们在形式化数学和代码等可验证领域看到了巨大进步，但在直觉性或无法形式化的领域进步将会停滞。这可能是真的。但是在数以百亿计的资金、成千上万顶尖头脑以及日益强大的模型倾注在这个难题上的情况下，这种心理安慰又能维持多久呢？

Perhaps the best counter-argument to runaway AI progress is that reinforcement learning does not generalize well, and that while we see immense progress in verifiable domains like formalized mathematics and coding, progress will stall in intuitive or unformalizable domains. That may be true. But with billions of dollars, thousands of brilliant minds, and increasingly capable models thrown at the problem, how long can that cope possibly last?

items.title: 📌 概要
items.text:
在这篇短文中，作者批判了我们将“不良激励”视为社会和个人失败根源的现代偏执。在承认扭曲的奖励结构无处不在的同时，作者认为归咎于激励机制是一种逃避——它暗示人类仅仅是被设定好去服从任意奖励系统的棋子。真正的正直、目标感和道德勇气要求我们超越系统本身，拒绝虚无的奖励追求，并培养我们内心的精神骨气。

In this essay, the author tackles our modern obsession with "bad incentives" as the root cause of societal and personal failures. While acknowledging that perverse reward structures exist everywhere, the author argues that blaming incentives is a cop-out—it implies that human beings are merely pawns programmed to obey arbitrary reward systems. True integrity, purpose, and moral courage require us to look past the system, reject hollow reward-seeking, and cultivate our own internal backbone.

items.title: 无论风浪多大，带上你自己的头盔
items.text:
大家想必都会同意：激励机制很糟糕。无论你看向何处，人们都在因做错事而获得回报。这已经成了解决所有问题的标准诊断，从气候变化到政治极化再到学术不端——“抱歉了伙计，你这是得了严重的不良激励病。”

We can all agree: the incentives are bad. Everywhere you look, people are being rewarded for doing the wrong thing. This has become the go-to diagnosis for every problem, from climate change to political polarization to scientific malfeasance—"sorry pal, you’ve got a bad case of the incentives."

我并不完全反对这种分析。谁能反对呢？这基本上是个同义反复：人们做坏事是因为他们做坏事得到了鼓励和奖励。 额，不然你为什么要做坏事呢？

I don’t disagree with this analysis, exactly. Who could? It’s basically tautological: People do bad things because they are encouraged and rewarded for doing bad things. Well, why else would you do them?

我对这种思维方式真正的抱怨在于，它暗示了激励机制应该被服从，服从它是正常的甚至是高尚的，而且除了服从之外别无选择。你又怎么能被期望为了——为了什么？为了做正确的事——而去打破规则、放弃晋升或牺牲哪怕零点几分的 GPA 呢？

My real gripe with this line of thinking is that it implies incentives should be obeyed, that it is normal or even noble to do so, and that it is perhaps impossible to do otherwise. How could you be expected to break a rule, forego a promotion, or give up a decimal of your grade point average for the sake of—what? Doing the right thing?

这里有一个原本不言而喻的道理，但现在却无人提及：激励机制是给输家准备的。 仅仅因为某个任意的奖励系统会给你一点甜头就去做某事——那是信鸽该干的事，不是人类该干的事。如果你围绕满足激励机制来构建生活，那你就是一个蠢货和傻瓜。

There’s a point here that should go without saying, but instead it has simply gone unsaid: incentives are for losers. Doing something simply because an arbitrary reward system will give you a lil treat—that’s for pigeons, not people. If you build your life around satisfying incentives, then you’re a dummy and a schmuck.

当我在少棒联赛打了几年灾难性的棒球时，我最不喜欢的部分就是上场击球，因为你必须戴上当地体育部门提供的那些破旧的击球头盔。没有一个是合身适尺寸的，而且闻起来就像有上百个汗流浃背的 10 岁小孩在你之前戴过一样。每一次击球不仅冒着被三振出局的风险，还冒着染上头虱的风险。

When I played Little League baseball for a few disastrous years, my least favorite part was going up to bat because you had to wear one of those ratty old batting helmets supplied by the local rec department. None of them fit right, and they all smelled like a hundred sweaty 10-year-olds had worn them before you. Every at-bat carried not only the risk of striking out, but also the risk of contracting head lice.

有几个孩子，那些认真的孩子，带了自己的头盔——量身定制，品味高雅地贴着贴纸，大概里面零头虱。这些孩子跑垒时就像小王子一样。

A few kids, the serious ones, brought their own helmets—custom fitted, tastefully decorated with decals, and presumably containing zero lice. These kids ran the bases like little princes.

我之所以说这些，是因为激励机制就像击球头盔：如果你不带自己的头盔，你就只能使用别人为你提供的破头盔。

I say all this because incentives are like batting helmets: if you don’t bring your own, you’ll have to use the crappy ones that are provided for you.

人类成长中至关重要的一部分——事实上，也是人类成长中最具“人性”的一部分——就是获得一个人生目标。如果你的道德信念本该存在的地方留有空白，那么你人格中的这个空腔就会被对金钱、权力、名声和地位的肿瘤般欲望所填满。这就是那种“对激励做出反应”的人。

A critical part of human development—in fact, the most human part of human development—is to acquire a purpose. If you have a void where your moral convictions should be, that cavity of your personality gets filled up with tumorous desires for money, power, fame, and status. This is the kind of person who "responds to incentives."

items.title: 救救我，上天的救星，你是我唯一的希望
items.text:
在没有经过任何正规指导的情况下，大约 100% 的人类都能学会说话，而大约 0% 的人类能自然学会阅读。说话轻松且早期就会；阅读出现得很晚且十分吃力，它依托于大脑中原本并非用于解码纸上符号的区域。

Without any formal instruction, approximately 100% of humans will learn to speak, while approximately 0% of humans will learn to read naturally. Talking comes easy and early; reading comes late and laboriously, piggybacking on bits of the brain that were never meant to decode squiggles on paper.

在思考任何人类能力时，问一个问题都很有用：这更像说话，还是更像阅读？

When thinking about any human ability, it’s useful to ask: Is this more like speaking, or is it more like reading?

建立价值体系似乎更类似于阅读。在 21 世纪初，社会学家 Christian Smith 和 Melinda Lundquist Denton 调查了美国青少年的宗教和道德信仰。他们得到的回应是一堆被他们称为“道德主义治疗型一神论”（Moralistic Therapeutic Deism）的废话。大多数青少年认为神基本上是一个飘在天空中的酷家伙，希望每个人都开心，充当着天上的管家，不需要太多其他东西。

Developing a value system seems to be a lot more like reading. In the early 2000s, sociologists Christian Smith and Melinda Lundquist Denton asked American teenagers about their religious and moral beliefs. What they got in return was a bunch of gobbledygook they termed "moralistic therapeutic deism." Most teens believed God was essentially a cool dude floating in the sky who wants everyone to be happy, acts like a celestial butler, and doesn't demand much else.

我们的价值体系脆弱，原因与我们的科学推理能力脆弱是一样的：在我们被告知认知模型崩溃之前，我们不会去修正它们。 除非你定期被投掷到伦理风暴中，否则没有什么能促使你巩固道德信念。因此，我们对对与错的认知很容易被任何还算过得去的奖惩机制所覆写，仅仅是因为我们心智的硬盘上原本就没有写下多少东西。

Our value systems are flimsy for the same reason our scientific reasoning is flimsy: we don’t fix our mental models until something tells us that they’re broken. Unless you are regularly thrust into ethical firestorms, there's nothing telling you to firm up your moral convictions. Consequently, our sense of right and wrong is easily overwritten by any half-decent system of rewards and punishments simply because we don't have much written there in the first place.

items.title: 你必须凝视这条怪鱼并走向狂乱
items.text:
你可以把 H.P. 洛夫克拉夫特（H.P. Lovecraft）的大多数短篇小说总结为：“这家伙看到了某个极其混乱可怖的东西，以至于他彻底疯掉了。”

You can summarize most of H.P. Lovecraft’s short stories as: "Guy looks at something so messed up that he goes totally bonkers."

这是一个非常有用的比喻，因为我认为在每个人心灵深处都有某种版本的“大怪鱼”（Big Horrible Fish）：某种未经审视的假设，如果你完全去审视它，就会要求你推翻自己生活的很大一部分。

This is a useful metaphor, because I think at the center of everyone’s psyche is some version of the Big Horrible Fish: some unexamined assumption that, if you fully considered it, would require you to upend a significant portion of your life.

我于 2021 年在旧金山参加一场学术会议时看到了我的那条“怪鱼”。在酒店内部，有数十场关于社会正义的演讲；而在酒店外部的 Tenderloin 街区，人们瘫倒在人行道上，死于药物过量。学者们急匆匆地从他们身边穿过前去发表论文——证实了心理学最著名研究之一所揭示的黑暗真相。

I saw my fish in 2021 in San Francisco, during an academic conference. Inside the hotel were dozens of talks on social justice; outside the hotel, in the Tenderloin district, people were sprawled on the sidewalk, dying of overdoses. Scholars scurried past them to present papers—proving a dark truth from one of psychology's most famous studies.

那天我心里的某些东西解扣了。我意识到我们并不是在寻求取得实际进展；我们只是为了自己的 CV 在发表论文而已。

Something un-clicked for me that day. I realized we weren't trying to make actual progress; we were just publishing papers for our CVs.

当我遇到拥有罕见正直品质的人——那些愿意不惜一切代价违抗激励机制的人时，我发现他们几乎总是目睹过那条“怪鱼”。他们经历了一场摧毁幻想的道德洗礼，并获得了锻造自身价值体系的机会。他们与输家截然相反。

When I meet someone of uncommon integrity—someone willing to defy the incentives at any cost—I find they almost always have seen the fish. They have undergone a moral reckoning that shattered their illusions and gave them the chance to forge their own values. They are the opposite of a loser.

items.title: 萨姆纳的 500 天
items.text:
我过去每天都会在我大学附近看到一个那样的人的雕像：参议员查尔斯·萨姆纳（Senator Charles Sumner）。

I used to see a man like that every day in statue form near my university: Senator Charles Sumner.

萨姆纳在波士顿的贫困环境中长大，生活在城市的黑人居民中间，并在 1830 年代前往法国旅行，在索邦大学看到黑人和白人学生作为平等的一员共同学习，这令他大吃一惊。他在日记中写道：

Sumner grew up poor in Boston, lived among the city’s Black population, and traveled to France in the 1830s, where he was astounded to see Black and white students studying together as equals at the Sorbonne. He wrote in his diary:

"那么，我们之间自由黑人与白人之间的差距必然源于教育，而非存在于事物的本性之中。"

"It must be then that the distance between free blacks and whites among us is derived from education, and does not exist in the nature of things."

他成为了他那个时代最直言不讳的白人废奴主义者。1856 年，在发表了一篇具有煽动性的反奴隶制演讲后，一位名叫普雷斯顿·布鲁克斯（Preston Brooks）的支持奴隶制的国会议员在参议院桌前走到萨姆纳面前，用手杖将他打得几近致死。

He became the most outspoken white abolitionist of his generation. In 1856, after giving an inflammatory anti-slavery speech, a pro-slavery congressman named Preston Brooks approached Sumner at his desk in the Senate and beat him nearly to death with a cane.

这是否吓退了萨姆纳？当他康复后，他变得更加激进，推动林肯废除奴隶制，并起草了 100 年后重新出现在《1964 年民权法案》中的修正案。萨姆纳很早就看到了那条“怪鱼”，并且他拒绝移开视线。

Did this deter Sumner? When he recovered, he became even more provocative, pushing Lincoln to abolish slavery and drafting amendments that would reappear 100 years later in the Civil Rights Act of 1964. Sumner saw the fish early on, and he refused to look away.

items.title: 停下脚爪，深思熟虑
items.text:
我理解为什么人们如此担心激励机制。看着恶人功成名就令人气愤。但古德哈特定律（Goodhart's Law）和坎贝尔定律（Campbell's Law）提醒我们，每一种激励机制注定最终都会被腐化。执念于激励机制感觉就像向“猴爪”许愿——它总是以讽刺的方式适得其反。

I understand why people worry so much about incentives. It’s infuriating to watch villains succeed. But Goodhart’s Law and Campbell’s Law remind us that every incentive is destined to be corrupted eventually. Obsessing over incentives feels like wishing on a Monkey's Paw—it always backfires ironically.

在试图修复激励机制的人与利用激励机制的人之间永恒的猫鼠游戏中，我支持猫。我们应该尝试完善我们的激励体系，但同时——别管什么激励机制，做正确的事。

In the eternal game of cat and mouse between those trying to fix incentives and those exploiting them, I am rooting for the cats. We should try to get our incentive systems right, but also—incentives be damned, do the right thing.

如果我们寻求终结我们的永久性难题，我们就必须在自己身上培养查尔斯·萨姆纳在领袖身上最看重的三样东西：

“第一是骨气（Backbone），第二是骨气，第三还是骨气。”

"The first is backbone, the second is backbone, and the third is backbone."

items.text: 长期以来，安全专家一直对租用用户网络连接的无牌电视流媒体盒发出警告。安全公司 Bitsight 的最新突破性调查揭示，包括 H96 在内的热门山寨电视棒（TV Streaming Sticks）已被秘密武器化，卷入了一场由 AI 驱动的大规模广告欺诈网络。当用户的电视关闭时，这些设备会伪装成知名品牌的手机，在 AI 生成的假冒网站上自动点击广告，为黑灰产团伙每天产生数万美元的非法收益，同时使用户的家庭网络陷入严重的安全风险之中。

items.title: 概要
items.text:
安全专家长期以来一直警告那些租用用户互联网连接的通用电视流媒体盒。然而，Bitsight 的一项突破性分析揭示，热门的无牌流媒体电视棒（如 H96）也被秘密武器化，卷入了一场由 AI 驱动的大规模广告欺诈行动。通过伪装成移动设备并利用自动化工作流，这些设备会在电视关闭时点击 AI 生成网站上的欺诈性广告，在给用户网络带来严重安全风险的同时，估计每天能为威胁分子带来超过 5 万美元的收益。

Security experts have long warned about generic TV streaming boxes that rent out user internet connections. However, a groundbreaking analysis by Bitsight reveals that popular off-brand streaming sticks—such as the H96—are also secretly weaponized in a massive, AI-driven ad fraud operation. By spoofing mobile devices and utilizing automated workflows, these devices click on fraudulent ads on AI-generated websites when the television is turned off, generating an estimated $50,000+ daily for threat actors while leaving user networks exposed to severe security risks.

items.title: 广告欺诈的隐藏机制
items.text:
安全公司 Bitsight 的威胁研究员 Pedro Falé 在收购了一个此前由 H96 流媒体电视棒用于遥测的过期域名后，揭开了这个复杂的广告欺诈网络。该域名定期从全球数万台设备收集硬件配置文件并安装应用程序。

Security firm Bitsight threat researcher Pedro Falé uncovered the complex ad fraud network after acquiring an expired domain previously used for telemetry by H96 streaming sticks. The domain periodically collected hardware profiles and installed apps from tens of thousands of devices worldwide.

然而，流量并没有显示为电视硬件，而是揭示出几乎所有的流媒体盒都在伪装成三星、Vivo、华为和小米等品牌生产的手机。

Instead of recognizing TV hardware, however, the traffic revealed that nearly all the streaming boxes were masquerading as mobile phones manufactured by brands like Samsung, Vivo, Huawei, and Xiaomi.

“我们注意到有些事情严重不对劲，” Falé 表示。“向这个工厂出厂预装的 Android TV Box 后门上报信息的多个设备居然都是‘手机’。”

“We noticed something was wildly wrong,” Falé said. “Multiple devices reporting to this factory Android TV Box backdoor were ‘phones.’”

items.title: 罪魁祸首：蜂窝集团（Fengwo Group）
items.text:
遥测数据指向了与浙江蜂窝物联网科技有限公司（以蜂窝集团/Fengwo Group名义运营）绑定的两个预装应用，该公司是一家成立于 2019 年的中国大陆企业。Bitsight 追溯了该行动在香港和新加坡的多个空壳公司身份。

The telemetry data pointed to two pre-installed apps tied to Zhejiang Fengwo IoT Technology Ltd (operating as Fengwo Group), a mainland China-based entity founded in 2019. Bitsight traced the operation back through various shell identities in Hong Kong and Singapore.

这些应用将 H96 流媒体电视棒作为被挟持的流量来源，访问由蜂窝集团创建的 AI 生成新闻和博客网站（涵盖金融、健康、游戏和美食领域）。关键在于，这些网站仅在由匹配被篡改的移动设备配置文件的受害流媒体棒访问时才展示广告。

The apps use the H96 streaming sticks as captive traffic sources to visit AI-generated news and blog sites (covering finance, health, gaming, and food) created by the Fengwo Group. Crucially, these sites only display ads when visited by a device matching the spoofed mobile profile of the compromised streaming sticks.

蜂窝集团的公开域名 (fwgcloud[.]com) 声称该公司专注于用于客户服务和情感陪护的“AI 数字人”。然而，Bitsight 发现的内部 Wiki 透露了一个更加实用主义的目的：利用 Google Blockly 视觉化编程语言的自定义实现来构建虚假网站。

The Fengwo Group's public domain (fwgcloud[.]com) claims the company specializes in "AI digital humans" for customer service and companionship. However, internal wikis uncovered by Bitsight reveal a far more utilitarian purpose: building sham websites using a proprietary implementation of Google’s Blockly visual programming language.

  • 低技术门槛操作人员： 使用 Blockly，低技能的操作人员只需拖放代码块即可定义自动化欺诈流程，而无需理解底层的技术细节。

  • Low-Skilled Operators: Using Blockly, low-skilled operators can drag and drop code blocks to define automated fraud routines without understanding the underlying technicalities.
  • Cost Efficiency: Templates created by expert developers allow the company to minimize technical overhead and operating costs.
  • Human-Like Navigation: When selected for a task, the streaming stick silently launches a browser, manages tabs, and uses vision-and-reasoning systems to identify and click ads just like a human user would.

Bitsight 发现，H96 设备会根据设备的使用状态在两种恶意角色之间切换：

Bitsight discovered that the H96 devices alternate between two malicious roles based on how the device is being used:

  1. 电视开机（HDMI 信号处于激活状态）： 该设备充当住宅代理（Residential Proxy），将其家庭互联网连接出租给匿名的第三方（从数据抓取者到网络犯罪分子不等）。
  2. 电视关机： 该设备切换任务以执行广告欺诈流程，确保繁重的计算处理不会干扰用户看电视时的正常视频播放。
  1. TV On (HDMI Signal Active): The device functions as a residential proxy, renting out the user’s home internet connection to anonymous third parties (ranging from scrapers to cybercriminals).
  2. TV Off: The device switches tasks to execute ad fraud routines, ensuring the heavy processing doesn't disrupt normal video streaming when the user is watching TV.

尽管 FBI 和安全行业领袖屡次发出警告，主要电商平台（如亚马逊、百佳、Newegg 等）仍在继续销售预装修改版 Android 系统的未经验证的廉价流媒体盒。

Despite repeated warnings from agencies like the FBI and security industry leaders, major e-commerce platforms (such as Amazon, Best Buy, and Newegg) continue to sell unverified, budget streaming boxes bundled with modified Android operating systems.

import subprocess
import json
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger("ai_insight")

def score_article(entry: dict, min_score: float = 30.0) -> float:
    content_text = entry.get("content") or ""
    char_count = len(content_text)

    if char_count < 2000:
        return 0.0

    prompt = (
        f"Evaluate this article:\n"
        f"- Title: {entry.get('title')}\n"
        f"- Author: {entry.get('author')}\n"
        f"- URL: {entry.get('url')}\n\n"
        f"Content Preview:\n{content_text[:3000]}\n"
    )

    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["agy", "run", "--skill", "skills/article-screener/SKILL.md", prompt],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=60
        )

        if result.returncode != 0:
            logger.error(f"Agent failed with error: {result.stderr}")
            return 0.0

        # Try to find JSON block in stdout
        import re
        match = re.search(r'\{.*\}', result.stdout, re.DOTALL)
        if not match:
            return 0.0

        data = json.loads(match.group(0))
        score = float(data.get("score", 0.0))
        reason = data.get("reason", "No reason provided")
        logger.info(f"Agent Evaluation Reason: {reason}")
        return score
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Exception calling agent: {e}")
        return 0.0

# Daily Publisher Orchestrator

You are the orchestration agent for ATBInsight's daily publishing pipeline. Your job is to execute the following three phases sequentially and fully autonomously. Do not stop to ask the user for permission between phases unless an unrecoverable error occurs.

## Phase 1: Ingestion & Screening
Run the daily ingestor script. This script automatically uses the Chief Editor skill to screen for high-quality articles.
**Command:** `bash -c "source /home/aitobox/miniconda3/bin/activate ATBInsight && python scripts/article_ingestor.py"`
Wait for this to complete. It will save the screened markdown files into `bak/origin/YYYY-MM-DD` (where YYYY-MM-DD is today's date).

## Phase 2: Translation & Categorization
Check the `bak/origin/YYYY-MM-DD` directory for new `.md` files.
If files exist, you must translate them using the `tech-article-translator` skill. 
Since there may be multiple files, **dispatch parallel subagents** (using your `invoke_subagent` tool) for each file or small batches of files, instructing them to:
1. Act under the `tech-article-translator` skill.
2. Read their assigned file from `bak/origin/YYYY-MM-DD/`.
3. Translate the content, extract a suitable category, and add relevant tags.
4. Add the standard YAML frontmatter.
5. Save the translated file to `docs/blog/posts/` with a renamed title format: `YYYY-MM-DD-Chinese_Title.md`.

Wait for all translator subagents to report completion before proceeding to Phase 3.

## Phase 3: Build & Deploy
Once translation is complete, you must update indices, build the site, and deploy.
Execute the following commands sequentially:

1. Generate chronological archive:
   `bash -c "source /home/aitobox/miniconda3/bin/activate ATBInsight && python scripts/generate_archive.py"`

4. Deploy to GitHub Pages:

items.text: The agent will act as the "ATBInsight Chief Editor". - Dislikes: Absolutely hates political content. Any hint of politics results in an immediate veto (0 score). - Loves: Deep tech, long-form, and highly substantive technical articles. - Appreciates: Humorous, geeky, and interesting tech news or culture pieces.
path: Article Screener Skill Design

items.title: Evaluation Mechanism
items.text: Instead of rigid formulas, the agent will rely on its persona to write a short "Editor's Monologue" (internal thought process) evaluating the article against its preferences. Based on this monologue, it assigns a holistic score from 0 to 100.
path: Article Screener Skill Design

items.title: Output Constraints
items.text:
To ensure the Python pipeline can parse the result reliably, the agent MUST output ONLY a valid JSON object without markdown code block backticks. Format: 

{
  "score": <0-100>,
  "reason": "<editor's monologue>"
}

items.title: Modification to score_article
items.text: The existing score_article function in src/robots/llm_robot.py (or moved to a new robot module) will be updated: 1. Remove HTTP API Calls: Strip out requests.post to OpenAI-compatible endpoints. 2. Subprocess Call: Use subprocess.run to execute: agy run --skill skills/article-screener/SKILL.md "Evaluate this article: [Metadata + Content]" 3. JSON Extraction: Use regex to extract the first valid JSON block from stdout. 4. Error Handling: If agy run fails, times out, or returns invalid JSON, log the error and default the score to 0.0.
path: Article Screener Skill Design

items.title: Logging
items.text: The ingestor will log both the numerical score and the extracted reason to provide clear visibility into the agent's decision-making process for each article.
